AI Search.description: Adds an AI search bar to the Jellyfin web client. Ask in natural language and get titles from your own library, personalized to your watch history. Also adds meaning-based matches inside Jellyfin's own native search, alongside title matches. Works with any OpenAI-compatible model, with a local or remote retrieval source.
AI Search.overview: AI natural-language search & recommendations from your own library.

versions.changelog: For Jellyfin 12. Jellyfin's own search now also finds titles by meaning, shown in the usual Movies, Shows and Episodes rows after the title matches. New options: turn it on or off, only use it for searches that look like a sentence, limit how many matches it adds, hide the AI search button completely (native search only), and keep a log of every search for a few days so an admin or API key can collect them.
Fixes the search button missing on new Docker installs.

One unified setup: a chat endpoint plus a local or remote retrieval source (replaces the old Direct/Platform modes). New: search without a language model, returning retrieval matches ranked by relevance with no per-result reasons. Embedding model is now a dropdown, and endpoints are configured per capability.
Show more now returns new titles instead of repeating the first results. Recommendations no longer come back empty on reasoning models.
Fixed a bug when choosing TV or Movies in platform mode.

AI Upscaler Plugin.description: AI-powered video upscaling plugin with Docker microservice architecture. Features automated hardware benchmarking, intelligent fallback system, pre-processing cache, and sidebar integration.
AI Upscaler Plugin.overview: Revolutionary AI upscaling plugin with Docker-based AI processing. Eliminates native DLL conflicts. Features comparison view, TV remote optimization, and sidebar integration.

versions.changelog: v1.8.3.35: The player button no longer needs write access to Jellyfin's web folder. The plugin adds its script to index.html as Jellyfin serves the page, so Windows installs (NetworkService), the Debian package, snaps and read-only containers get the button in every browser tab. Behind a Jellyfin base URL, the Lanczos, Anime4K and WebGPU real-time engines load again. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.34: Real-time upscaling starts again in the web client. Since v1.8.3.31 it refused every video with "Video color metadata unavailable", because Jellyfin 10.9 and later no longer put the playing item in the page address; the player now reads the item from the video's stream or the web client's playback request and checks the version that plays. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.33: Redesigned in-player menu and settings page. SDR videos (DVD/SD rips, untagged 10-bit) are no longer refused as HDR in real time or in library jobs; HDR batch output keeps the model's detail; Server AI hides stale frames during outages and falls back to Lanczos when the server cannot keep up. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.32: Native Jellyfin 12 build on .NET 10, aligned plugin/test dependencies, updated CI and ABI-aware release validation. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.31: Remove the image-action rate limit from playback frames/chunks; forward busy/error responses and Retry-After; serialize player captures with abortable requests and backoff; guard driver upscaling and object masking; enforce measured Auto-mode performance; reject invalid model categories and unsupported HDR; fail library jobs on AI errors without local resize/original-frame substitution; enforce nonempty passing TRX and publish-only runtime packaging. Target-server acceptance was explicitly waived by the owner; GPU, live-player and HDR target-hardware behavior remain unverified.

v1.8.3.30: notifications stack instead of piling up - issue #77, 'if you hit a toggle in quick succession, the notifications at the lower right side of the screen will simply pile on top of each other'. They did, literally: every notification was its own position:fixed element anchored to the same corner, so two of them resolved to the identical coordinates and the second covered the first. Measured in a browser against the real CSS - three toasts all reported top 1185 / bottom 1226; after the fix 1185, 1136, 1087 with no overlap. They are flow children of one fixed host now and the host does the stacking, column-reverse so the newest sits nearest the corner. Two things beyond the literal report, both aimed at what 'quick succession' actually produces: a repeated toggle emits the SAME text over and over, so an identical message already on screen has its timer restarted instead of being cloned (firing 'Settings saved!' five times leaves one), and the stack is capped at four so holding a control down cannot fill the viewport. THE PLUGIN HAD THREE COPIES of this code, each with the same defect - the config page (reported), the player overlay and the quick menu - and all three are fixed, because patching only the reported surface is how the same bug gets filed twice. sidebar-upscaler.js was already correct (it defers to Jellyfin's own toast module) and a test now keeps it that way. Verified by measurement, not by reading: a browser harness built from the real CSS and the real showToast confirmed stacking, de-duplication and the cap, and re-applying the old position:fixed rule reproduced the exact overlap from the screenshot. Eleven regression tests; five reintroduced defects are each caught. 375 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.29: the error message now says what went wrong. Testing v1.8.3.28 live showed the last piece of the same problem - a failed Load Detection Model printed one generic sentence regardless of cause, because the handler read err.responseText (an XHR field) while Jellyfin 10.11's client is fetch-based. Checked against the running server rather than assumed: the rejection is [object Response], err.text IS a function, err.responseText does not exist, status 404 - so JSON.parse(undefined) threw on every failure and the fallback was the only thing anyone saw, while the body carried exactly what was needed ('... is not on disk. Import or upload a detection model first'). That reaches the status line now. The same run confirmed the v1.8.3.28 modelName parameter end to end: the service named the id that was passed, not the saved one. The old fallback also advised saving the settings first, which stopped being true in v1.8.3.28 when the button began saving them itself. 364 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.28: the two object-masking UI bugs reported in discussion #11, where the feature itself is confirmed working - Ultralytics YOLO exports load (YOLO26n fastest in the reporter's testing), boxes land where they should, 5-10 fps at low quality on a Ryzen 5 7600 through docker7-cpu. 'THE STATUS WOULD OFTEN STICK ON A PREVIOUS MODEL NAME' - because it was telling the truth: the button POSTed nothing and the endpoint read only the SAVED config, so a newly typed id loaded the PREVIOUS model and the status correctly named that one. A comment in the UI described this exact trap and guarded only against an empty field; documenting a bug is not fixing it. The endpoint takes a modelName parameter now, the button sends what is on screen, and the saved value stays as the fallback for scripts. 'IT SEEMED TO IGNORE THE CONFIDENCE VALUES I PUT IN' - it did. step=0.05 makes a type=number input report value === '' for entries the browser rejects, and floating point puts ordinary values off that grid: (0.6-0.05)/0.05 evaluates to 10.999999999999998, so 0.6 was rejected. The save path skipped empty strings, which normally means 'left blank' but here meant 'the browser disliked it', so the number vanished without a word. Now step=any, parsed and clamped, and the stored value written back into the field. Both share a root cause: an action button sits next to fields that were not persisted until the global Save, so Load Detection Model now saves the card first - which also stops values reverting when you navigate away and back. Four regression tests, each verified to fail when its fix is reverted. 364 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.27: three defects a live server showed that no unit test could. EVERY TRANSLATED STRING HAS BEEN FALLING BACK TO ITS KEY on every install since the i18n work landed - strings.en.json is declared as an EmbeddedResource, MSBuild lists it as one, and it was not in the DLL, because MSBuild reads the '.en.' in the file name as a CULTURE TAG and compiles it into a satellite assembly the release ZIP does not ship. Jellyfin logged 'Failed to get resource' on every config-page load. The test guarding it asserted that the .csproj MENTIONED the file, which it always did; it now reads the built assembly's manifest resource names, and removing the fix fails it. /hardware-info REPORTED THREE THINGS IT NEVER CHECKED: GpuAvailable returned the HardwareAcceleration config toggle (default on), so a CPU-only server was told it had a GPU while /gpu-verify on the same box reported no devices at all; FFmpegAvailable was the literal true and OnnxRuntime the literal 'Available'. All three are observations now, null means 'not asked yet' rather than 'no', and what the user requested is a separate field. THE FRAME PROXIES THREW AWAY THE DIAGNOSIS: after a container restart the service answers {'detail': 'No model loaded'} and both proxies replaced it with 'Frame upscaling failed'; confirmed that was all it was by loading fsrcnn-x2 and getting 200 at 4.7 fps / 214 ms per frame at 480x270 on a CPU-only box. Also two documentation errors found the same way: GET /Upscaler/health is listed and does not exist (only health/detailed), and benchmark-frame is a GET, not a POST. 360 C# + 166 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.26: the plugin downloads the detector itself - tiny-yolov3 is a catalog entry now, so the Models tab fetches and verifies it exactly like an upscaler instead of asking you to bring your own. That became possible only once the pin could be VERIFIED rather than asserted: the file was downloaded, its sha384 checked against the OpenVINO model zoo's own model.yml, and the catalog's sha256 computed from those exact bytes. A REAL MODEL FOUND A REAL BUG: loading the actual tiny-yolov3 on a live server reported input_size 640, because the export declares its spatial dims as ('N', 3, None, None) - nothing in the file says 416 - so the loader used the generic fallback while the anchors are trained for 416. The code was right and the result was wrong; every synthetic test model declares a fixed size, so no test could reach that path. The catalog carries net_size 416 and the loader prefers it. Also two bugs in the catalog sync script, found by running it: it EXECUTED main.py to read the model list (needing fastapi, OpenCV and ONNX Runtime) and had failed outright since v1.8.3.23 with 'attempted relative import' after `from . import object_mask` was added - it parses with ast now; and it would have collapsed the pretty-printed catalog onto one line, because PowerShell captures output as an array and Out-File -NoNewline joins array elements with no separator. 356 C# + 166 Python green.

v1.8.3.25: detection models could not be imported AT ALL - reported in discussion #11 and it was my bug. The import gate hard-required a 4D output, so every detection model was rejected with 'Expected 4D output (N, C, H, W), got shape [1, None, 4]' - the boxes tensor of exactly the yolo-v3-tiny export object masking was built for. v1.8.3.24 could load a detector and mask with it, and there was no way to get one in; every test for that release started from a model already sitting in the models directory, so none walked the path a user walks. The fix is a shared gate rather than an override switch: the importer classifies the model - 4D in and 4D out is an upscaler, otherwise it asks object_mask.plan_for, the SAME function that decides how to drive it at load time. A model that imports is a model that loads; a laxer separate check would only move the rejection to a later step, which is worse because by then the user believes it is installed. An imported detector registers as object-detection with no scale factor, so it stays out of the upscaler dropdowns and auto-mode cannot pick it for a video, and the category survives a container restart. A model that is neither is refused with BOTH readings explained. Six tests cover import to load to mask as one path; against the old gate five of them fail with the reporter's exact message. NOTE: the fix lives in the AI service - update the Docker image too. 354 C# + 166 Python tests green. Also fixes two shutdown bugs found by installing this build on a real server: VideoProcessor released the processing permit as the first statement of its finally block, so on shutdown ObjectDisposedException skipped the rest of the cleanup and a clean stop was logged as a processing failure; and a progress update to an already disposed SessionManager logged a warning with a stack trace on every shutdown with a running job. 356 C# tests green.

v1.8.3.24: object masking now runs DURING PLAYBACK - the part of discussion #11 that v1.8.3.23 did not deliver. That release shipped the masking as a service endpoint nothing called, while the request was for a real-time filter; the user could already produce the result externally, live during playback was the whole point. The player's capture loop already existed for server-side upscaling - it pulls frames off the video element and draws the result onto an overlay - and masking simply had nowhere to send them. Enable it in Settings (classes, box or blur, padding, confidence) plus an admin-gated button that loads the detector, or toggle it live in the player menu under Auto - Cover objects. It REPLACES real-time upscaling while running: upscaling and detecting is two full inference passes per frame, which no realistic server sustains at playback rate, and both surfaces say so rather than letting you discover it as stutter. Batch upscaling is untouched. Padding defaults to 12px because a detector's box hugs the animal and the ears sticking out set a dog off just as well. No detection model ships with the plugin - every catalog entry carries a verified sha256 pin. TESTS THAT CAN ACTUALLY FAIL: mutation testing on v1.8.3.23 found two guards asserting text rather than behaviour - the neighbouring-directory bypass could be fully reintroduced with the suite green (the test asserted the source contained 'rootWithSep', which the bypass leaves in place), and the critical path check was guarded by counting occurrences of IsInsideMediaLibrary( so making the call unreachable kept both the count and the green suite. Both are exercised now: the containment rule is a tested function and ProcessVideo is called with a mocked library manager. The same pass deleted a state field written but never read, and the AI service's masking endpoints are now driven end to end by real synthesised ONNX models, one per detector family. Also: a CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md the contributing page had been linking to while the file did not exist, and every site page showed the current version in the topbar and v1.8.3.13 in the footer - eleven releases stale, because the sync script and the audit both only looked at the topbar. The class list is URL-encoded and confidence formatted invariantly, so 'dog&mode=blur' cannot become a second query parameter and de-DE cannot send 0,35. 354 C# + 160 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.23: object masking, the answer to discussion #11 - a user's dog reacts to dogs and cats on TV and asked for ffmpeg's dnn_detect + drawbox via a custom -vf chain. That cannot work here: jellyfin-ffmpeg's build carries 46 --enable-* flags and no DNN backend at all (no libopenvino/libtensorflow/libtorch, the string 'dnn' does not appear in it), so those filters are absent from the ffmpeg Jellyfin ships whatever the plugin passes. Arbitrary -vf would also be a hole rather than a feature - ffmpeg filter syntax includes movie= and subtitles=, which read files, handing every authenticated user the same primitive v1.8.3.22 just closed on POST /process. So it is done in the AI service, which already loads ONNX models per frame: POST /models/load-detector loads a detector alongside the upscaler rather than instead of it, and POST /detect-mask covers detections with a filled box or a blur, by COCO class or the 'animals' group, with padding because a detector's box hugs the animal and the ears sticking out set a dog off just as well. No detection model ships with it - every catalog entry carries a verified sha256 pin and inventing one would break exactly the guarantee the importer provides, so users bring their own through the existing upload/import path. The decoder handles the v3/v5/v7 and v8/v9 layouts and refuses anything else, because a misread tensor does not throw, it paints boxes over the wrong part of the picture. Also: the face-restore preview proxy read request bodies into the Jellyfin heap unbounded and is now capped at 32 MB, and a static check over the whole AI service asserts every global name its code references exists - written because the detector loader called a helper this service has never had, which Python resolves at call time, so the module imported cleanly and the endpoint would have raised NameError the first time anyone used it. 321 C# + 140 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.22: code-review fixes - one critical and nine confirmed high findings, each re-verified against the code first. SECURITY: POST /process accepted any path on the server (the controller carries only [Authorize] and, unlike its two siblings, had no media-library allowlist) - with ffmpeg's -y an arbitrary-overwrite primitive, plus a file-existence oracle; there is one shared separator-safe allowlist now and neither job entry point overwrites an existing file. AUTO MODE WAS NEVER RUNNING IN BATCH: Model defaulted to realesrgan-x4 while the nightly scan gates on 'auto enabled and model empty or auto', so that gate was always false and every batch run skipped the hardware cap and 8K guard while the dashboard displayed Auto - the default is empty now and the dropdown finally offers Auto. LOCALE: fps= and both -ss values used the current culture, so on de-DE/fr-FR 23.976 became fps=23,976 and a comma is the ffmpeg filter separator - every frame-by-frame job on those servers failed. QUEUE: two permit leaks plus an empty-queue branch that handed the surplus back = 100% of a core after any cancel. Three silent misreports fixed: a Lanczos fallback stored as an AI result (which made the scan filter skip that image forever), an HDR URL that 404'd on a trailing slash while reporting success, and expired cache entries orphaning multi-GB files. And cleanup-dockerhub-tags would have deleted all 71 current tags and re-pointed :latest to a v1.7.8 image - the version is derived from meta.json now. 14 regression guards; 315 C# + 123 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.21: maintainability groundwork - two structural packages, nothing user-facing. model_import.py is a verbatim extraction of the OpenModelDB import and pth->ONNX conversion block from main.py (6808 -> 6627 lines): byte-identical function bodies, no route moved, the endpoints keep their decorators. Three test monkeypatch targets moved with it, and one had been passing for the wrong reason. i18n groundwork makes English a SOURCE language read from Configuration/strings.en.json via a small t() helper - adding a locale is copying the file, translating values and one line of code. Nothing was translated; this phase proves the structure. The scope was cut deliberately: a full extraction is ~485 strings with no user-visible benefit until a translation exists, and the existing UI guard checks element ids rather than text, so a botched sweep would ship silently. 58 keys are migrated - the activity strip and auto-mode texts, all new or rewritten in v1.8.3.20. A missing key renders as the key name rather than an empty string, and t() takes a fallback so the first paint never flashes key names. docs/I18N.md records the numbers and how to continue. 300 C# + 123 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.20: honesty, visibility, reproducibility - five packages, no features. The UI promised 'AI picks model + filter per video' and the code half-kept it: auto stopped overwriting a chosen preset in v1.8.3.14 but still wrote its own whenever the field was empty, so the first playback quietly decided your look. Auto now never writes a filter at all - it offers one in the player's Auto tab and the sidebar with an Apply button, and only when its opinion differs from yours. The activity strip is one line stating phase, frame x of y, model with the auto reason, fps and ETA; those numbers were computed every frame and discarded, and the old 'N jobs completed' counted a list that never contains completed jobs. docs/ENDPOINT-AUDIT.md reports all 66 routes against their real callers (20 unreferenced, grouped by what they are - including six Processing Queue endpoints the settings page configures but no UI ever calls). /Upscaler/hardware-benchmark retires the misleading /Upscaler/recommendations name, which stays as a deprecated alias with an identical payload. Reproducible builds finally are: lock files existed since v1.8.3.13 and no image installed one; five variants now install hash-pinned locks with --require-hashes, and intel and nvidia produced their first lock ever. The Python suite had been red since v1.8.3.14 and shipped over six releases because pytest was not a gate - it is now, and the download path plus the SSRF gate have real coverage. 293 C# + 123 Python tests green.

v1.8.3.19: the Auto tab no longer states a default as a fact. Browser-testing the new tab against the live server caught it reporting 'RUNNING NOW / nomosuni-compact-x2 / HD content in real time' on a page where no video was playing: with no video element the resolver is handed 0x0, falls through to its HD branch, and the pane presented that fallback as a decision about the file in front of you - while also printing the literal string 'unknown output size' as though it were data. Three headings now, matched to what is actually known: 'Running now' when a video is playing and auto is on, 'Auto would pick' when auto is off, and 'Default pick - start playback for this file' when there are no dimensions to decide from. In that last state the output size and the resolution-derived reason are omitted rather than printed, because both would be fabricated; the model, its scale and the signals list stay, because 'Resolution: unknown' is true and useful. Verified in a real browser against the deployed plugin: Auto leads the tab bar, all four switches render their config state, and toggling face restoration flipped EnableFaceRestore, persisted it and re-rendered the pane. 273 tests green.

v1.8.3.18: Auto mode gets its own tab in the player. Auto has been the default since v1.8.3.12, but the in-player panel only ever asked the Custom-mode questions - pick a model, pick a filter - and could not answer the one that matters while a video is running: what did auto decide for THIS file, and how do I turn it off without leaving the player. The panel now leads with an Auto tab showing the model, its scale, the resulting output size, the reason, the signals it looked at and any substitution warning, plus live switches for auto mode, video filters, face restoration and real-time upscaling - each takes effect immediately, and 'Re-apply to this video' re-runs the decision against the running upscaler. The filter row states what is true: auto suggests a look and never overwrites a preset you chose. Docs caught up too: site/configuration.html described auto-selection with models that are not in the catalog (hat-x4, swinir-m-x4, realesrgan-x4plus) and a genre mapping the resolver never had; it now carries the real decision table plus the hardware-budget and scale-ceiling filters. README gains an Auto Mode section. 273 tests green.

v1.8.3.17: 4K sources are cleaned up, not enlarged. TargetScaleFor has answered 1x for sources that are already 4K since v1.8.3.14, but nothing acted on it - only the substitution filter read it and no branch ever produced a 1x pick, so a 4K source still went to 7680x4320. There is now an explicit branch ahead of the multi-frame and anime paths: a 4K source gets a 1x restoration model that removes compression artefacts at the original size. Second cause: the scale parser knew only the 'x<N>' order (realesrgan-x4) and not the '<N>x' order used by the 1x restoration models (dejpg-realplksr-1x) and by every OpenModelDB import (omdb-4x-nomos8k-atd), so every 1x model reported unknown scale; both are parsed now, end-anchored first so realesrgan-x4-256 still means 4x. The overshoot test theory now includes 4K - leaving it out is what hid this - and states the honest invariant: exceeding the target factor must be a reported substitution carrying a reason. 273 tests green.

v1.8.3.16: a substitution must not overshoot the target size. The quality ladder added in v1.8.3.15 picked by weight alone, so a branch that had deliberately chosen a 2x model for 1080p was handed clearreality-x4 - cheap, Light and 4x - producing 7680x4320 with the branch's own reason text ('a 4x pass would target 8K for no visible gain') printed next to it; a 4K source reached 15360x8640. A substitute now has to fit the hardware AND stay within the resolution's target factor, and when nothing satisfies both, the affordable candidate with the smallest scale wins so the overshoot is as small as available. Branch fallbacks are still tried before the ladder, and an id that encodes no scale is not rejected because unknown is not the same as too big. SD keeps its full 4x restore. 270 tests green, including a theory across weak-cpu/strong-cpu/igpu x 720p/1080p x live-action/anime asserting no pick ever exceeds its target factor.

v1.8.3.15: three defects that only a real machine could show, found deploying v1.8.3.14 to a CPU-only server. PreferredAnimeModel shipped with a default of anime-compact-x4, and the resolver cannot tell a shipped default from a deliberate user choice - which is exempt from the hardware budget and the scale logic by design - so EVERY anime decision skipped both and a CPU-only box got a 4x model on 1080p (7680x4320); the default is now empty like its live-action counterpart (saved values are kept: set Preferred Anime Model back to Auto if you never chose one deliberately). The v1.8.3.14 8K fix only covered live action - anime batch still targeted 8K on 1080p. And the budget fallback only walked a branch's own candidates, none of which contain a light model, so on a weak CPU every live-action job collapsed to the last-resort fsrcnn-x2 while clearreality-x4 is equally cheap, does 4x and is ~32x faster than realesrgan-x4 per CPU tile; there is now a quality ladder within each weight class. Reasons describe the material instead of naming a model, so a reason can no longer advertise something that was substituted away. 266 tests green.

v1.8.3.14: Auto mode respects your hardware, and tells the truth about scale. The content heuristic and the AI service's hardware advisor were two separate recommenders that never spoke to each other, so a CPU-only NAS could be handed a full restoration net; the hardware class is now cached and an over-budget pick falls back with a stated reason (an unknown class caps nothing, and a model you picked yourself is never overridden). The service ignores the requested scale and uses the model's native factor, so the library scan logged scale=2x while auto ran a 4x model - a 1080p batch job silently produced 8K frames; the real factor is now read from the model, reported by the API, used by the job, and a 1080p batch no longer defaults to 4x. Every downloadable catalog model gets a Get button (27 of them had none) with real byte progress, and 'Not DL' is split into 'Not downloaded' vs 'Self-host only'. Pause/Resume/Cancel added to the dashboard activity strip. Auto mode no longer overwrites a filter preset you chose. Batch runs log their model reasoning at Information instead of Debug. Stray scrollbar next to the tab row removed. 262 tests green.

v1.8.3.13: Auto mode explains itself + reproducible builds. The automatic model choice now returns Reason, Signals and SubstitutedFrom instead of writing them to a debug log that is off by default: the dashboard shows Auto -> model with the reason, an expandable list of what it looked at, and an amber warning when a preferred model was substituted (Custom mode is labelled honestly instead of advertising an unused pick). New activity strip joins running file, phase, progress and model into one line (paused jobs shown as paused). The sidebar's hardware recommendation carries a reason too. Build side: APP_VERSION defaults removed from all 7 Dockerfiles (six said 1.8.2, one 1.8.3.8 - the service reported a wrong version) with a release-guard assert, new weekly lock workflow resolving each Python layer inside its real base image, and CI now builds five image variants per push instead of one. New docs/DOCKER-IMAGES.md with real image sizes and the AMD stack CVE + exit trigger. Tests: xUnit 199, pytest 112.

v1.8.3.12: Dashboard Auto/Custom mode switch (Auto default: model+filters picked per video from benchmarks). Numeric sliders reverted to number inputs (toggles stay). Live Benchmark card below Face Restoration; stable benchmark boxes. FACE FIX: gpen-512 + restoreformer++ re-pinned after upstream re-uploads (gate had refused correctly) - all four face models download/load now. Console: 5000-line buffer + Download; FBGEMM hint. pytest 103, xUnit 190. Docker lockstep v1.8.3.12.

v1.8.3.11: Settings redesign + async everything + player favorites. NEW 'Models' tab bundles catalog, star-favorites, importer (incl. file-install), face restoration, benchmark and comparison in one place; the Settings tab shrank to five labeled groups with a live settings search. All 19 checkboxes render as toggle switches, 8 numeric fields became sliders with value badges (same ids - saved configs untouched). Imports/conversions run as background jobs with honest phase reporting (no more proxy timeouts on big CPU conversions); face-restore models (~300 MB) download in the background with live status. The in-player quick menu shows your star-pinned models first, and imported models can be deleted from the Favorites card. Tests: pytest 103, xUnit 190. All 7 docker images in lockstep as v1.8.3.11.

v1.8.3.10: Import-UX hotfix (plugin-only). The 'permanent red messages' were mostly a design bug: the NC license notice was rendered in the same red as real errors - now amber with 'import still possible' wording; red is reserved for real failures. Every import/install failure line now says what to do next (service unreachable -> check URL; timeout -> retry or file-install; 401/403 -> token mismatch; 501 -> converter image needed). Favorites card no longer briefly shows 'not on the service' for a just-imported model (render-order fix); the Model Catalog title shows the real count instead of a stale '(35 Models)'. Docker images in lockstep as v1.8.3.10.

v1.8.3.9: Hotfix from the first live server run of the v1.8.3.8 importer/converter. ZIP imports (AnimeJaNai) failed because OpenModelDB pins the INNER .onnx, not the zip - the extractor now selects the member matching the catalog pin. pth conversion failed on torch >=2.9 (dynamo exporter needs onnxscript) - the export now pins the legacy exporter and the converter image ships onnx+onnxscript. Both were refused cleanly by the verification gates instead of installing wrong bytes. pytest 99, xUnit 190. All 7 docker images in lockstep.

v1.8.3.8: Install ANY OpenModelDB model. v1.8.3: Opt-in pipeline parallelism (plugin-only, no Docker change). New experimental setting 'Pipeline parallelism' (default OFF) overlaps frame extraction with upscaling instead of running them strictly back-to-back: while ffmpeg is still extracting later frames, already-extracted frames are upscaled concurrently. Built on a thread-safe FrameStreamCoordinator that hands a frame to the upscaler only once a successor frame proves it was fully written, and drops the unproven highest frame if extraction fails, so the output frame-count and ordering are identical to the sequential path. Default behaviour is unchanged; the overlap runs only when the box is ticked. Works with the existing docker7 AI-service images (no rebuild needed). Tests: xUnit 164 (incl. (3) entrypoint.sh detect_backend() now knows WSL2 /dev/dxg so the startup banner no longer falsely says 'Backend: cpu' on WSL2 setups where main.py correctly detects the GPU. v1.7.6: Intel OpenVINO Provider Hotfix. Closes the last open Point of issue #69 (Intel Arc GPU detected but inference ran on CPU). Root cause: requirements-intel.txt had a wrong comment claiming onnxruntime-openvino was deprecated and that plain onnxruntime + system OpenVINO would work; in reality, plain onnxruntime from PyPI does NOT bundle the OpenVINOExecutionProvider, even with system OpenVINO present in the base image. After Docker Hub rebuild + container restart, /gpu-verify shows OpenVINOExecutionProvider as active provider and Intel GPU is actually used for inference. (3) FIX ProcessingStrategySelector substring-matcher tightened: removed broad 'compact' and 'realplksr' matchers that falsely accepted anime-compact-x4 (anime-category) and nomos2-realplksr-x4 (video-quality) for RealTime, causing frame drops. (4) FIX 4 sync File.Copy in frame-loops (VideoFrameProcessor + ProcessingMethodExecutor) replaced with async streaming. Pattern from v1.6.1.20 CacheManager:307 fix extended to all hot-paths. (6) FIX UpscalerController filter-preset list deduplicated 4x to 1x via new _validFilterPresets static readonly. (7) HONEST 6 unimplemented dead-config toggles (EnableModelPreloading, EnableHealthMonitoring, EnableModelAutoCleanup, EnableQualityMetrics, EnableFaceEnhancement, EnableGrainManagement) now flagged in XML-doc as 'currently no-op pending v1.7.0 pipeline implementation'. v1.6.1.20: Adoption Completion + Cancellation + Async-IO. Follow-up patch closing the gaps the v1.6.1.19 post-release self-audit found. (1) FIX HardwareBenchmarkService.cs:123 - status.CurrentModel was bypassing EnsureModelAvailable via ?? null-coalescing; now wrapped. (2) FIX UpscalerCore.cs single-frame returns (7 sites) now route through PickAvailable for defensive symmetry with multi-frame paths (no behavior change today, regression-guard for future). (3) NEW BUG CLASS: 9x HttpClient GetAsync/PostAsync in UpscalerController got HttpContext.RequestAborted - prevents 120s hangs when client disconnects. (4) NEW BUG CLASS: CacheManager.cs:307 synchronous File.Copy replaced with async streaming via FileStream + CopyToAsync (useAsync:true) - was blocking thread-pool thread for 5-30s on NAS-mounted disks. (6) +7 new tests SingleFramePaths_AlwaysRouteThroughPickAvailable covering all 7 single-frame branches. dotnet build 0/0 errors, dotnet test 72/72 (was 65). No model changes, no schema changes, no breaking config - v1.6.1.19 saved configs are bit-for-bit compatible.

v1.6.1.19: Structural fix release closing the drift class that v1.6.1.17 and v1.6.1.18 patched point-by-point. (1) NEW Services/ModelAvailability.cs - single source of truth (HashSet + IsKnownUnavailable + PickAvailable) consumed by both UpscalerCore (refactored, kept logging-wrapper) and HardwareBenchmarkService (new EnsureModelAvailable helper hardens 7 previously-unguarded hardcoded model assignments). (2) FIX Face-Restore dropdown was hardcoded HTML <option>s for gfpgan-v1.4 / codeformer. Now auto-populated from /Upscaler/models category=face_restore — symmetric to the v1.6.1.17/18 main + anime/live-action dropdowns. (3) FIX Homepage card on site/index.html showed the v1.6.1.16 FFmpeg-fix text under a v1.6.1.18 header (pauschal version-bump bumped <h3> title without rewriting body); rewrote card with actual release content. (4) NEW <InternalsVisibleTo Include='JellyfinUpscalerPlugin.Tests' /> grant in csproj so tests directly assert on the internal ModelAvailability contract. (5) NEW JellyfinUpscalerPlugin.Tests/Services/ModelAvailabilityTests.cs +28 tests with explicit drift-locks (HaveCount(5), NotContain('realesrgan-x4')) + case-insensitivity + null/empty handling + PickAvailable semantics. dotnet build 0/0 errors, dotnet test 65/65 (was 37). No model changes, no schema changes, no breaking config — v1.6.1.18 saved configs are bit-for-bit compatible.

v1.6.1.18: Follow-up patch to v1.6.1.17 fixing 3 sibling bugs caught by external audit. (1) FIX PreferredLiveActionModel was Dead-Config (defined, UI dropdown, persisted, but never read by ResolveModelForVideo) — exact symmetric twin of the v1.6.1.17 PreferredAnimeModel fix that Verifier-A/B both missed. New non-anime override hook with PickAvailable fallback (override → ultrasharp-v2-x4 → nomos2-realplksr-x4 → realesrgan-x4). Setting Preferred Live-Action Model in Settings now actually does what the UI says. Updated to v1.6.1.18 + new section recommending publicly-available drct-l-x4 over self-host nomos8k-hat-x4 and real-cugan-x4 over gated apisr-x3. (4) NEW TEST UpscalerCoreAutoModelTests.cs +1 [Theory] LiveAction_NonAnime_NeverReturnsKnownUnavailableModel locks down the live-action path symmetric to the anime drift-protection. Verification: dotnet build 0/0 errors, dotnet test 37/37 (was 33). No new models, no schema changes, no breaking config — v1.6.1.17 saved configs are bit-for-bit compatible.

v1.6.1.17: (1) FIX Auto-Mode broken for multi-frame VSR — ResolveModelForVideo() in UpscalerCore returned animesr-v2-x4 / realbasicvsr-x4 / edvr-m-x4 unconditionally, but all three are available:False (self-host required). New PickAvailable() helper now skips known-unavailable models and falls back to single-frame equivalents (realesrgan-animevideo-x4 / ultrasharp-v2-x4 / nomos2-realplksr-x4). (3) FIX site/models.html drift — listed 8 fictional models (waifu2x-cunet, hat-l-x4, swinir-l-x4, realesrnet-x4plus, ...) that never existed in the registry; now auto-generated from AVAILABLE_MODELS via Scripts/sync-fallback-models.ps1. (4) FIX Anime default model changed from "" (which fell through to self-host VSR in auto-mode) to anime-compact-x4 (5MB, available=true). v1.6.1.16: Hotfix for issue #64 — LibraryUpscaleScanTask was failing on every item with two related cold-start errors ("File not found: ffprobe" → then after partial fix "Cannot start process because a file name has not been provided"). Root cause: THREE singletons (VideoAnalyzer, VideoFrameProcessor, ProcessingMethodExecutor) all captured empty ffmpeg/ffprobe path strings at plugin construction time, before Jellyfin's MediaEncoder finished resolving /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/{ffmpeg,ffprobe}. Fix: new EnsureFFmpegReady() in VideoProcessor re-resolves EncoderPath/ProbePath on demand, reconfigures FFMpegCore's GlobalFFOptions, and pushes the resolved paths into all three sub-services via new UpdateFFprobePath() / UpdateFFmpegPath() methods. Called at top of ProcessVideoAsync / ExtractSingleFrameAsync / ExtractSingleFrameWithFiltersAsync so scheduled tasks work even when the plugin boots before MediaEncoder. Verified live on Jellyfin 10.11.8 — scan task now extracts frames at 31% progress where previously it was 0/70 success. README header synced 1.6.1.14 → 1.6.1.16 (was missed in v1.6.1.15).

v1.6.1.15: In-player panel redesigned from AI-gradient/neon to a clean operator dashboard (Docker-Dashboard palette: #0b0d12/#11141b surfaces, #3b82f6 accent, underline tabs, monospace numerics). New live status strip at the top of the quick-menu: active-dot + state (ACTIVE/STANDBY/IDLE/DISABLED) + mode (Server/WebGL) + FPS + active model — polls every 500ms while menu is open so you can see whether upscaling is actually running. Docker AI service operator console redesigned (Grafana/Linear/Vercel): sticky topbar with live status dot + auth-posture chip, 4 tabs, KPI tiles, inline SVG latency sparkline from /metrics, model catalog with search+filter, hardware panel, API browser from /openapi.json + live Console tab that streams service logs via SSE. NEW Auto-Mode (default OFF under Settings → Auto Model Selection): when enabled, the plugin calls /Upscaler/recommend-model on playback start and picks both model and color-filter preset per video — anime → animesr-v2-x4/anime-compact-x4 + vivid, horror/thriller → drama, sci-fi → cyberpunk, documentary/low-res → sharp-hd, multi-frame batch → edvr-m-x4/realbasicvsr-x4. Override is session-only; saved preferences are preserved. Library-Scan codec picker expanded 3 → 12 options with per-codec encoder defaults. Player FPS HUD auto-hides in sync with Jellyfin's OSD fade.

v1.6.1.14: Select Library feature (issue #64) — scheduled library scan can now target specific libraries instead of always scanning everything. New chip-based library picker on Settings tab; new GET /Upscaler/libraries endpoint enumerates virtual folders; EnabledLibraryIds config field persists selection. Empty = legacy scan-all behavior. Bugfixes: saveConfig now actually writes EnabledLibraryIds (was missing from save payload, so selection silently reset every save); PluginVersion hardcoded string + header-meta + sidebar JS + csproj AssemblyVersion all synced 1.6.1.13→1.6.1.14 (previously save wrote old version back, plugin looked permanently one version behind). Docker AI service UI (localhost:5000): API_TOKEN-not-configured shows a single dismissible banner instead of repeat-spamming toasts; toast dedup 10s window + max-3 stack + click-to-dismiss; model search + status filter. FastAPI /status exposes api_token_configured/auth_enabled. Live-tested: all 26 config-page buttons across 6 tabs with 0 console errors.

v1.6.1.13: In-player quick-menu redesigned + live filter controls. The overlay that pops up from the Upscaler button during playback is now a tabbed interface [Models | Filters | Realtime] instead of a flat scroll. New Filters tab lets you tune the video look WITHOUT leaving playback: pick any of 15 preset looks (Cinematic, Vintage, Vivid, Sepia, Cyberpunk, Teal&Orange, ...) or drag 3 live sliders (Brightness / Contrast / Saturation) — the <video> element's CSS filter property updates at ~60fps for instant feedback, no re-transcode. An Advanced collapsible exposes server-side params (Gamma, Sharpness, Color Temperature, Vignette, Film Grain, Denoise) that persist via new POST /Upscaler/filter-config endpoint and kick in via FFmpeg on next seek. Reset/Save on both tiers. LIVE indicator dot pulses green while the CSS overlay is applied. Live sliders work fully offline — no AI service required; only the advanced FFmpeg params need the filter chain path.

v1.6.1.12: Bugfix + model-catalog cleanup. (1) gfpgan-v1.4 + codeformer URLs repointed from the never-published kuscheltier/jellyfin-vsr-models repo to the public facefusion/models-3.0.0 mirror — both flipped to available:true. (2) RIFE frame-interpolation replaced: old rife-v4.6 / rife-v4.6-lite pointed at a 404 v0.0.0 placeholder tag — now rife-v4.9 (quality), rife-v4.8 (balanced, new), rife-v4.7 (fast) from yuvraj108c/rife-onnx. (4) New Scripts/verify-release.ps1 runs end-to-end post-release validation: SHA against live manifest, ZIP-contents scan for forbidden patterns (Moq/Mono.Cecil/CodeCoverage/.pdb/.deps.json) that caused the v1.6.1.11 wrong-ZIP-upload bug. AniLiberty STRM 2.0.0.15 — Jellyfin 12

### Changes

- Added support for Jellyfin 12.
- Reduced unnecessary artwork downloads during library updates.
- Reduced background processing for intro and outro skipping.
- Fixed a problem that could remove generated library files when AniLiberty returned incomplete data.

### Upgrade Notes

Restart Jellyfin after updating. No settings changes or library regeneration are required.

AniLiberty STRM 2.0.0.14 — Jellyfin 10.11

### Changes

- Reduced unnecessary artwork downloads during library updates.
- Reduced background processing for intro and outro skipping.
- Fixed a problem that could remove generated library files when AniLiberty returned incomplete data.

### Upgrade Notes

Restart Jellyfin after updating. No settings changes or library regeneration are required.

Release 2.0.0.13
AniLiberty STRM Performance Update

This update makes library generation and Skip Intro/Outro processing faster and lighter on Jellyfin, especially for larger libraries.

### Performance Improvements
- Faster full-catalog and Favorites library generation.
- Reduced CPU and memory usage during generation and library updates.
- Faster preparation of native Skip Intro/Outro data after Jellyfin starts or scans a library.
- Improved performance during repeated scheduled runs and when multiple library locations are configured.
- Reduced memory usage while processing artwork and plugin-managed library data.

### Upgrade Notes
- Restart Jellyfin after installing the update.

Release 2.0.0.12
AniLiberty STRM Native Media Segments & Docker Playback Hardening

This release improves Jellyfin-native skip controls, managed-library refresh behavior, authentication visibility, and Docker playback safety. It also expands automated coverage and adds formatting/analyzer checks to both stable and nightly release pipelines.

### Licensing and Branding
- The repository is now licensed for non-commercial use under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0**.
- Added explicit commercial licensing, trademark, and required-notice documents.
- Commercial use requires separate permission from the project owner; the AniLiberty STRM name and branding are not granted for unrestricted reuse.

### Docker Direct Play Guard
- Fixed automatic playback proxy URL selection inside Docker and other containers.
- The plugin no longer writes container-only bridge addresses such as `172.17.x.x` into generated `.strm` files.
- Proxy base URL priority is now: explicit **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL**, `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl`, then native-host auto-detection outside containers.
- When no client-reachable HTTP(S) base URL exists in a container, generation safely falls back to direct AniLiberty HLS URLs and records a clear task warning.
- Invalid manual or published proxy URLs are ignored instead of producing broken playback links.

### Native Skip Intro / Outro
- Replaced generated EDL and chapter XML skip files with a Jellyfin `IMediaSegmentProvider` implementation.
- Opening and ending timings are stored in `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/media-segments.json` and exposed as native Jellyfin media segments.
- Added background warm-up and path-to-episode reconciliation so existing library items receive updated skip timings without rewriting user-authored metadata.

### Managed Mirror and Metadata Refresh
- Expanded managed manifest tracking for STRM, NFO, artwork, popularity metadata, and media-segment state.
- Generated metadata is refreshed when the upstream AniLiberty signal changes while unmarked user-authored files remain protected.
- Cleanup remains bounded to plugin-managed files, with `Keep`, `DryRun`, and opt-in `Delete` behavior.
- Improved specials, franchise-season, fractional-ordinal, hydration, and image-handling paths.

### Popularity and Authentication Visibility
- Added an optional AniLiberty popularity badge to Jellyfin Web item pages.
- Added a public, read-only metadata endpoint backed only by plugin-generated popularity sidecars.
- Added Jellyfin activity notifications when a stored AniLiberty token starts returning HTTP 401/403, with cooldown protection against notification spam.
- Improved login/password, OTP, favorites, and watch-timecode API handling and validation.

### Playback and Sync Reliability
- Kept HLS playlist and segment delivery streaming through Jellyfin without buffering complete media objects in memory.
- Improved STRM URL normalization, playlist route handling, redirect validation, and playback diagnostics.
- Improved per-session watch-progress coordination, cancellation, path resolution, and forward-only progress updates.

### Quality Gates and Verification
- Added `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` to stable and nightly workflows, covering formatting and built-in Roslyn analyzer diagnostics without an extra linter dependency.
- Expanded automated coverage across controllers, API clients, scheduled tasks, managed cleanup, native media segments, popularity injection, authentication notifications, and Docker proxy URL selection.
- Full release-gated result: **207/207 non-integration tests passed**, clean Debug and Release builds, and zero compiler warnings. Three opt-in live AniLiberty API checks remain outside the release gate.
- Reproduced the Docker failure on Jellyfin 10.11.11: an internal bridge URL caused `DirectPlayError` and ffmpeg fallback; a client-reachable proxy URL played the same H.264/AAC stream through Direct Play with no transcoding.

### Upgrade Notes
- Restart Jellyfin after installing the update.
- Run **Generate AniLiberty STRM library** again so existing `.strm` files and managed state receive the new routing and metadata behavior.
- Docker users who want Jellyfin-proxied playback should set **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL** or `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl` to an address reachable by playback devices and the Jellyfin container.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build.
- No full-segment server-side cache or mid-segment resume; brief client-side HLS buffering remains the current protection against connection jitter.
- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts or the legacy GitHub Pages repository URL.
- No season-gap fix: the reported missing-season case was not established as a plugin defect in this work.

Release 2.0.0.9
AniLiberty STRM Hardening System Release

This update hardens AniLiberty STRM Plugin as a full Jellyfin reconstruction system: stable Jellyfin ABI targeting, explicit AniLiberty identity, safer generated-library governance, streaming playback proxying, and a stronger operational surface for administrators.

### Jellyfin Compatibility & Quality Gates
- Pinned all `Jellyfin.*` NuGet references to `10.11.0` to stop builds from silently drifting to newer Jellyfin packages.
- Added committed `packages.lock.json` files and locked restore in CI.
- Added CI checks that verify every resolved `Jellyfin.*` package remains on `10.11.0` while `targetAbi` stays `10.11.0.0`.
- Release automation now keeps `build.yaml`, package version, assembly version, file version, and informational version in sync.

### AniLiberty Identity & API Courtesy
- Rebranded the public plugin identity to **AniLiberty STRM Plugin** while keeping the legacy `AniLibriaStrmPlugin` repository URL for install compatibility and branch history.
- Added a shared `PluginIdentity` with display name, product token, repository URL, version discovery, and canonical User-Agent.
- All AniLiberty API, media proxy, static media, and HLS clients now identify as:
  `AniLibertyStrmPlugin/<version> (Jellyfin; +https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin)`.

### Mirror Governance Layer
- Added `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/manifest.json` inside each output root to track files managed by the plugin.
- The manifest records generated STRM, ANIID, EDL, chapter XML, NFO, artwork/thumbs, release/episode IDs, hashes, sources, and timestamps.
- First manifest run initializes the baseline and never prunes existing files.
- Generated NFO/artwork refreshes only when the file is known as plugin-managed through the manifest or generated marker.
- Existing unmarked `.nfo` files and artwork are preserved as user-owned content.

### Safe Cleanup Modes
- Added `StaleCleanupMode`: `Off`, `DryRun`, and `Delete`.
- Default is `DryRun`, which reports stale managed files without deleting anything.
- `Delete` removes only manifest-managed stale files and then removes empty directories created by that cleanup path.
- Untracked user files are left alone.

### Playback Proxy Rail
- Non-playlist HLS segments and keys now stream directly to `Response.Body`.
- The proxy no longer reads segment/key payloads into memory with `ReadAsByteArrayAsync`.
- Upstream host allow-listing and redirect validation remain in place.
- Playlist rewriting continues to route segments and keys through the Jellyfin proxy endpoint.

### Identity & Access Command Center
- OTP codes are no longer persisted in plugin configuration after the OTP flow.
- Login/password and OTP sign-in clear stored OTP state.
- The token box is masked by default, with explicit reveal/copy actions.
- Auth logs no longer include the login e-mail address.

### Operational Reliability
- Scheduled tasks now rethrow failures after logging so Jellyfin can mark task execution accurately.
- Cancellation flows are preserved instead of being swallowed as generic failures.
- AniLiberty progress pull no longer overwrites newer local Jellyfin playback positions with older remote timecodes.
- Clearing UI logs now persists the cleared state.

### Presentation & Documentation
- README now presents the plugin as a coherent product system: Signal Acquisition Layer, Context-Aware Reconstruction Core, Playback Proxy Rail, Mirror Governance Layer, Operational Command Center, and Distribution Quality Gates.
- Added three README visual assets showing the reconstruction core, system capability layers, and operational command center.

### Test Coverage
- Added tests for Jellyfin package pins and lock-file resolution.
- Added User-Agent and named/static HTTP client coverage.
- Added managed mirror tests for baseline creation, generated metadata refresh, unmarked NFO preservation, dry-run cleanup, delete cleanup, and empty-directory cleanup.
- Added proxy tests for streaming segments, playlist rewriting, unsupported upstream rejection, redirect validation, and upstream failure status.
- Added auth/config tests for OTP payload boundaries, safe defaults, and AniLiberty identity.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build in this release.
- No migration of AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.
- No destructive cleanup unless `StaleCleanupMode` is explicitly changed to `Delete`.

# AniLiberty API v1 Alignment, Better Metadata & Quieter Logs

This update improves AniLiberty authentication reliability, aligns the plugin with AniLiberty API v1 responses, and enhances generated metadata while keeping UI logs under control.

## Authentication & OTP
- Improved login and OTP endpoints with proper HTTP status codes and safer request validation.
- Updated OTP parsing to support the API v1 format (`otp.code`) and kept backward compatibility for older responses.
- OTP flow in the settings UI is simplified to **Start → Sign In** (the “Accept OTP” UI action was removed).

## Networking reliability
- Switched API calls to a reusable, DI-managed `HttpClient` (`IHttpClientFactory`) with consistent headers (User-Agent / Accept / Accept-Language).
- Added retry handling for rate limits (**HTTP 429**) and transient errors.
- Optimized HTTP reads using `ResponseHeadersRead` to reduce overhead and improve responsiveness.

## STRM generation & metadata quality
- Better year handling for AniLiberty v1 (`release.year` instead of `season.year`), including TV show year selection across grouped seasons.
- More accurate content classification:
  - Detects **MOVIE** by API `type.value` when available.
  - Routes **SPECIAL / OVA / OAD** into **Season 00** more reliably.
- Improved image handling:
  - Supports v1 image schema (`preview/thumbnail/optimized`) and prefers non-optimized URLs when possible.
  - Normalizes `.webp` URLs to `.jpg` and safely determines thumbnail file extensions even when URLs contain query parameters.
- Episode NFO improvements:
  - Writes episode titles (RU/EN when available), runtime, year, and sets `lockdata=false`.

## Logging & settings
- Added **“Enable debug logs (very noisy)”** setting:
  - When OFF: DEBUG/TRACE aren’t stored in UI logs and per-title progress logging is throttled to avoid bloating the UI log.
- UI log filtering now respects minimum log level and the debug toggle.

## Developer / maintenance
- Manual generation test is now **skipped by default** and uses environment variables (`ANI_TOKEN`, `ANI_OUTPUT_DIR`) so tokens aren’t stored in the repo.
- Internal null-safety improvements around plugin initialization.

## Not included
- No changes to library scanning behavior or broader UI redesign beyond the OTP/auth/logging settings shown above.

AnimeClick Metadata.description: Provider metadati anime in italiano basato su AnimeClick.it con scraping etico e cache locale.
AnimeClick Metadata.overview: Fornisce titoli, trame, generi, valutazioni e cover art in italiano per anime, utilizzando AnimeClick.it come fonte.

versions.changelog: Major per Jellyfin 12 e .NET 10, verificata su 12.0 e 12.1. Interfaccia riprogettata con guida iniziale, preferenze semplici e strumenti avanzati separati. Identificazione automatica più prudente fra titoli simili, remake e stagioni; correzione manuale cercando il titolo in libreria e incollando il link AnimeClick, senza cancellazione diretta delle immagini. Corretti redirect di rete, collisioni e scadenza della cache, concorrenza nei refresh, rate limit e coerenza della coda traduzioni. AI opzionale e disattivabile senza perdere il profilo; impostazioni e credenziali esistenti conservate. 210 test backend per versione server e 11 test browser. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo: non installare su 10.11; le release precedenti restano disponibili. Dettagli e limiti delle verifiche nel rapporto di audit della release.

AniList ha disattivato la propria API e risponde 403 a chiunque. Il plugin ci riprovava a ogni elemento della libreria, due volte per elemento, pagando ogni volta il ritardo fra le richieste e scrivendo centinaia di avvisi identici. Ora dopo tre fallimenti di fila le chiamate vengono sospese e si riprova dopo cinque minuti, poi dieci, venti, fino a un'ora, con un solo tentativo alla volta; al ritorno di AniList l'interruttore si riarma da solo. Un rate limit o un annullamento non contano come fallimento, e con le richieste sospese non viene scritta alcuna cache negativa. Titoli, trame, generi e cast non dipendono da AniList e non cambiano.

AnimeClick e' passato a Bootstrap 5 e la ricerca non trovava piu' nulla: ogni query tornava zero risultati, in silenzio, quindi nessun titolo aggiunto dopo il cambio del sito poteva essere riconosciuto. Ripristinati ricerca, staff e opere collegate. La ricerca ora ripulisce i nomi delle release, accorcia il titolo finche' non trova, e rifiuta gli abbinamenti deboli invece di prendere il primo che capita. Se AnimeClick ha la scheda ma non la trama, la sinossi italiana arriva da TMDB. Le fixture dei test sono HTML scaricato dal sito, cosi' un prossimo cambio di markup si vede subito.

Via il tetto di 200 episodi: il ricontrollo dei titoli lavora tutto l'arretrato, protetto dal ritardo fra le richieste. I titoli mancanti sono divisi fra recuperabili, in attesa della fonte e non recuperabili. La pagina perde contatori e pulsanti superflui: i numeri filtrano con un clic e la selezione manuale resta solo sui titoli incerti.

Completare le sinossi è un clic solo: «Completa tutte le sinossi» avvia un'attività che procede a lotti e si ferma da sola quando non resta niente su cui agire, continuando anche a pagina chiusa. La stessa attività è pianificata ogni settimana.

Le sinossi degli episodi tornano anche per gli anime lunghi tenuti in una sola stagione: il numero assoluto pubblicato da TheTVDB viene letto senza richieste aggiuntive e su TMDB viene tradotto nella coppia stagione/episodio reale, solo quando la coordinata richiesta non può esistere.

L'audit ricorda l'esito di ogni riparazione: le sinossi che nessuna fonte ha escono dal lotto automatico invece di essere riproposte a vuoto, quelle in attesa di traduzione non vengono riaccodate e il lotto si distribuisce fra le serie.
Audit libreria più leggibile su desktop e mobile, con ricerca, filtri, sezioni progressive e controlli bulk sicuri per titoli e sinossi.
Audit qualità della libreria e riparazione sicura delle sinossi; abbinamento episodi e stagioni più rigoroso; coda traduzioni AI resiliente con refresh Overview-only; cache e invalidazione corrette.

v0.5.0.0: rilascio di funzionalità. La traduzione automatica non è più legata a un solo fornitore: il servizio si sceglie da un menu fra Ollama (in rete o in casa), OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Together, xAI Grok, LM Studio o qualunque endpoint compatibile OpenAI. Il nome del modello non ha più un valore predefinito, di proposito: i fornitori li ritirano e rinominano, quindi il plugin chiede l'elenco al servizio con il pulsante «Elenca modelli». Chi aveva già configurato Ollama non deve fare niente, il profilo salvato viene travasato al primo avvio. Non è possibile usare un abbonamento ChatGPT o Claude al posto di una chiave API: l'API è fatturata a parte e Anthropic vieta l'uso dei token dei piani consumer fuori dai suoi programmi. Nuova scheda Libreria: analizza la copertura dei titoli leggendo solo le schede già in cache, quindi senza richieste ad AnimeClick, e per ogni serie e stagione dice quale delle nove cause spiega un titolo mancante, con i pulsanti per rileggere la scheda, svuotarne la cache o avviare subito il ricontrollo. Il ricontrollo settimanale ora sceglie con la stessa classificazione, invece di spendere il budget sulle schede che non pubblicano titoli e di ignorare per sempre gli episodi mai abbinati. Corretti due abbinamenti: uno spin-off numerato nella stessa tabella azzerava le coordinate di ogni riga (27 titoli irraggiungibili su una sola serie) e gli extra numerati oltre la serie regolare non venivano più trovati. Timeout della traduzione portato a 90 secondi: il tetto di 30 tagliava richieste sane.

v0.4.5.0: rilascio di correzioni, tre difetti trovati provando il plugin su una libreria reale. Le sinossi italiane da TheTVDB non hanno mai funzionato: la pagina episodi veniva scartata per una forma di risposta assunta male, e su otto serie di prova TheTVDB aveva 119 sinossi italiane su 212 episodi, tutte irraggiungibili. Le sinossi di AnimeClick mancavano su ogni episodio con un accento nel titolo, perché l'identificativo salvato veniva rifiutato dal plugin stesso: il 13% degli episodi in prova. Una stagione intera poteva ricevere i titoli sfalsati di una posizione quando la tabella di AnimeClick contiene più righe di quante ne dichiari: ora la discordanza viene rilevata e serve la conferma del titolo del file, altrimenti l'episodio resta intatto. Inoltre: i titoli che ripetono solo il numero non vengono più scritti, la coda delle traduzioni non può più fermarsi in silenzio, e verso TheTVDB, TMDB e AniList c'è un passo minimo con rispetto delle richieste di rallentamento.

v0.4.4.0: audit del codice in tre giri, senza nuove funzionalità. Correttezza: le righe “Speciale” non diventano più episodi numerati con l'anno (prima spostavano la numerazione degli episodi successivi o rompevano la divisione automatica in stagioni), e il filtro sulle locandine a bassa risoluzione non si disattiva più da solo. Sicurezza: allow-list host HTTPS su tutti gli URL immagine (serie, film, episodi, stagioni e anteprime di ricerca), tetto di 15 minuti al Retry-After del server per non bloccare lo scraping fino al riavvio, impostazioni validate sul server e non solo nella pagina di configurazione. Robustezza: timeout e limiti di dimensione su tutte le chiamate di rete, budget sul recupero della lista episodi di TheTVDB, token TheTVDB scartato quando viene rifiutato invece di essere riusato per 24 ore, errori di chiave API e di rete ora visibili nel log invece che solo a livello Debug, un errore di scrittura della cache non fa più perdere i metadati dell'elemento, e cache per le foto degli autori.

v0.4.3.0: voce del plugin nella sidebar del pannello di controllo; banner del footer mostrato per intero; fix SSRF sugli URL immagine di serie/film (allow-list host HTTPS); HttpClient via IHttpClientFactory per evitare collisioni tra versioni; rimozione di memory leak nei lock, pulizia dello stato più efficiente e parsing/regex indipendenti dal locale; modello Ollama Cloud predefinito ora gpt-oss:20b-cloud con migrazione automatica.

v0.4.2.0: AnimeClick diventa la prima fonte per le sinossi degli episodi, ignorando descrizioni vuote, segnaposto e commenti; fallback TheTVDB/TMDB/Ollama, matching indipendente dai titoli, cache e diagnostica aggiornate; README riscritto per l'utente finale.

v0.4.1.0: Resolver episodi/stagioni v5 fail-safe con layout multipli, separazione tra episodi regolari e speciali, override deterministici e cache single-flight; diagnostica e frontend aggiornati con banner/footer; documentazione Ollama EN→IT ampliata.

v0.4.0.0: AnimeClick-first con authority layer lock-aware, resolver stagioni v4, metadati semantici estesi, coda asincrona Ollama con backoff e cache content-addressed, e fix E14-E26 per stagioni sintetiche.

v0.3.8.0: Fortificazione e ottimizzazione ricerca metadata. Filtro qualità immagini: MinPosterWidth (default 400px, ora in UI) — se AnimeClick fornisce locandina (o artwork) a bassa risoluzione viene automaticamente saltata e Jellyfin passa ad altri provider configurati (Fanart/AniList/TMDB). Probe efficiente con HTTP Range + cache. Search: cleaners robusti (sequel, fullwidth, &), scorer fuzzy migliorato, retry transienti nel client. Bugfix: versioning assembly corretto, UA dinamico, TvdbLanguage sanitizzato, Person images Order=100. Aggiornamenti UI e docs.

v0.3.7.0: Fix multi-stagione quando AnimeClick elenca episodi in blocco unico (es. The Asterisk War 24ep/2cour). Parser sintetizza SeasonNumber da <dt>Stagioni</dt> main-page. Matches S2 via seasonOrdinal.

v0.3.6.0: Fix TVDB tvdb_id restituito come stringa (API v4 /search) + fallback al campo id. Gestione accenti italiani in ricerca AnimeClick (RemoveDiacritics su query e scorer). Timeout 30s su IdentifyAndRefresh con risposta graceful. Ollama ParseTranslatedContent gestisce \uXXXX e surrogate pairs. Attribution TheTVDB (banner config + README).
v0.3.5.0: Fix TVDB search (type=series filter broken in v4 API, filter client-side).

v0.3.4.0: Fix HTTP 415 sui pulsanti Test TMDB/Ollama/TVDB e Svuota cache. I POST dal frontend venivano inviati senza body e senza Content-Type, causando 415 da ASP.NET Core prima di contattare le API esterne.
v0.3.3.0: Update logo to gatto.png and change title to AnimeClick Plugin

v0.3.2.0: Remake completo del frontend con architettura modulare in stile KometaThemes. CSS esterno (ac- design system, palette arancione), JS esterno (form dinamici, dirty-state, toast, modal), HTML bootstrapper minimale. Quattro tab (Overview, Metadati, Sinossi, Strumenti), hero con stat tile, sticky save bar, feature chips, provider test con live dot. Ogni impostazione mappata 1:1 al backend.

v0.3.1.0: Fix download immagini. GetImageResponse ora invia User-Agent/Referer (il CDN AnimeClick rifiutava le richieste senza UA → HTTP 403, locandine e foto staff non scaricate). Nuova opzione MinPosterWidth: scarta le locandine sotto la risoluzione minima e passa al provider successivo (Fanart/TMDB/AniList).

v0.3.0.0: Redesign completo del frontend — premium dashboard UI. Nuova interfaccia glassmorphism con gradienti animati, tipografia premium, micro-interazioni fluide, nuovi bottoni e badge. UX/UI migliorata con card più eleganti e layout rivisitato.

v0.2.11: Nuova dashboard premium glassmorphism con header sticky, tab bar iconata a pillole, tile stato provider, azioni rapide e save dock fisso. Ricerca impostazioni live e descrizioni toggleabili. Backend invariato.

v0.2.9: TheTVDB come fonte preferita per le sinossi degli episodi in italiano, con traduzione diretta e zero carico sul NAS. Se TVDB non ha la traduzione, il plugin usa il fallback TMDB piu Ollama Cloud. Aggiunti i pulsanti di test TMDB, Ollama e TVDB per verificare le credenziali inserite con messaggi di errore dettagliati.

v0.2.10: Pagina di configurazione rinnovata. Quattro schede in alto (Metadati, Sinossi episodi, Ricerca, Strumenti) con card visive e icone. Rimossa la sezione diagnostica tecnica, sostituita da strumenti piu semplici: Identifica e Aggiorna, e Svuota cache con un clic. I test di connessione TMDB, Ollama e TVDB ora mostrano un badge Connesso o Errore invece del testo tecnico. Risolto il bug dei pulsanti di test che mostravano parentesi vuote.

v0.2.8: AnimeClick ora fornisce solo i campi in italiano (titolo, trama, generi, tag, cast) e lascia agli altri provider i campi neutri come studio, anno e valutazione. Aggiunta la locandina italiana di AnimeClick come immagine di fallback quando AniList, Fanart o TMDB non hanno immagini. Sinossi degli episodi in italiano opzionali via TMDB piu Ollama Cloud.

v0.2.7: AniList ID risolto durante OGNI scan, non solo nell'Identify manuale. Nuovo servizio AnimeClickAniListResolver (estratto da AnimeClickIdentifyController, registrato in DI, DRY). SeriesProvider e MovieProvider ora risolvono e scrivono ProviderIds[AniList] in GetMetadata a ogni scansione, usando il titolo originale (romaji) con fallback al titolo italiano: le pagine AnimeClick non espongono link MAL/AniList/AniDB/TMDB, quindi questo fallback e cio che permette all'ImageFetcher AniList di scaricare le copertine in automatico e fornisce ai provider a valle un ID stabile. Nota: Fanart per i film usa il TMDB ID, quindi abilita anche TheMovieDb come metadata fetcher nella libreria Anime Movie. Controller rifattorizzato per riusare il servizio + nuovi unit test su parsing JSON ed escaping GraphQL.

v0.2.6: Fix response body undefined (client JS leggeva PascalCase, ASP.NET Core serializza in camelCase) + fix RemoteImageQuery che passava providerName=string.Empty (filtrava per provider con nome vuoto, ritornando array vuoto per Primary/Backdrop/Logo/Art/Thumb). v0.2.6.0 usa providerName: null (tutti i provider) + IncludeDisabledProviders=true. Nuovo EnsureAniListIdAsync che interroga AniList GraphQL per titolo e salva l'AniList ID sull'item prima del download immagini (necessario perché AnimeClick non fornisce TMDB/IMDB/AniList ID, quindi senza AniList ID l'AniList ImageFetcher non può fare lookup). DownloadedImages list ora visualizzata in modo leggibile nel result box della configPage.
