Artwork Generator.description: Artwork Generator is a Jellyfin plugin that automatically creates custom episode posters using smart frame analysis, black frame detection, and configurable text styling. Perfect for filling in missing or generic episode artwork with clean, consistent visuals.

versions.changelog:
## Features
- Frames are no longer taken from inside media segments, so intros, credits, recaps, previews, and commercials stay out of generated artwork
- New Avoid Media Segments setting under Frame Extraction, with a checkbox for each kind of segment to avoid, all on by default
- Segments come from a media segment provider turned on for the library, so items without any extract as before

## Developer
- Changing which segments are avoided discards the idle frame pools, so the next refresh extracts under the new choice

## Features
- New Cleanup Backdrops scheduled task under Library that reduces every item on the server to a single backdrop, keeping the first and deleting the rest along with their files
- The task has no default schedule, so it only runs when started by hand or on a trigger you add

## Features
- Primary and thumb images can name a second and third design, adding their versions of the same frames to the Edit Images picker
- New Edit Images Cache setting for how long rendered choices stay available, default 30 minutes
- Edit Images reuses the choices it already rendered when switching image type or page, instead of rendering every image again

## Fixes
- The Edit Images cache is bounded by size at 256 MB and releases expired images on its own, instead of holding them until the next render
- Every design in one Edit Images render draws from the same frames, even while other items are extracting
- Posters pass over a logo Jellyfin only knows by web address and use the next logo that can be read

## Developer
- Settings saved before 12.0.2.0 are no longer brought forward, so update through 12.0.2.1 first when coming from an older version
- Code, pages, and docs say logo rather than series logo, since films draw their own

## Fixes
- The Profiles page loads again instead of failing on a backdrop setting that no longer exists
- Posters with a logo draw the logo selected for a film, season, or series instead of falling back to text

## Features
- Artwork Generator is Episode Poster Generator rebuilt, with the same settings and a much wider job
- The repository moved with the name; re-add it as jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator to keep getting updates
- Draws posters, thumbs, backdrops, and text logos, where before there were only episode posters
- Covers series, seasons, films, music videos, home videos, and anything else with a video
- Configuration is rebuilt in three parts, designs, logos, and profiles
- Profiles decide which items get which images and which design draws each one
- Every design renders portrait and landscape, so one design covers a tall poster and a wide thumb
- A design's two lines are now simply the title and the subtitle, whatever the item is
- Text position and alignment work on every design, not just the few that had them
- New Bloom design, pooling color from the frame behind the text
- New Grid canvas, tiling several extracted frames into one picture
- Logo designs build a text logo from any name field, with letter case, a line limit, and frame-filled letters
- Frame extraction is one set of server settings instead of a copy on every design
- Frames are ranked on tone, detail, contrast, and color rather than just clearing a threshold
- Optional setting drops a subtitle that only repeats the title
- A subtitle too long to fit can shorten to its code, shrink, or trim
- Two example designs per style, each showing a genuinely different look

## Fixes
- Seasons extract from their own episodes instead of falling back to the series backdrop
- Candidate images come from different episodes instead of clustering in one
- Heavily letterboxed frames scale back up to a usable size
- Portrait text is measured against both sides, so it no longer reads small
- Brush strokes stay thick on tall posters instead of piling into a cross
- Long titles trim at a word boundary rather than mid-word
- Descenders stay inside the safe area
- Borders, rules, and shadows scale with the poster
- A static graphic keeps its proportions
- An item with no name of its own says its one line in the larger type
- Generated images carry the item's metadata language

## Developer
- The generator, the settings model, and the configuration page are rebuilt around item kinds rather than episodes
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 that Jellyfin 12.0 ships
- Designs are found by reflection, so adding one needs a class and an enum value
- Every label, option, and default is read from the settings models
- The shared generator is split into pipeline, text, and overlay
- Frame analysis is a single pass, under a megabyte per frame instead of three and a half
- Every one-time upgrade of an older configuration sits in its own file, to be deleted whole once installs have moved on
- Tests hold the documentation, the templates, and US spelling to the code

## Features
- Shadows, rules, and the Frame border now scale with the poster, so they read the same on a 4K frame as on a DVD rip instead of turning into a hairline or a slab
- Long titles that do not fit two lines fill the first line with whole words and trim only the second, at a word boundary, instead of cutting both lines mid-word

## Fixes
- Frame drew no border at all for an episode without a name, and ignored the Show Title setting
- Cutout no longer lets a two line title run into the bottom of the cutout letters
- Split center-crops the series poster into its panel instead of stretching artwork that is not 2:3
- Brush honours the Show Episode setting and keeps a wrapped title inside the area the strokes leave clear
- Timeline keeps the marker dot inside the safe area on the first and last episode
- Text blocks are reserved from the font's real ascent and descent, so descenders no longer hang past the safe area

## Developer
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 packages Jellyfin 12.0 ships, since the plugin binds to the server's copies at runtime
- Text drawing moved from the removed SKPaint text members to SKFont, wrapped in a shared TextStyle so every style measures and draws with the same objects
- Standard and Split share one text stack; Numeral, Cutout, Brush, and Frame no longer hand-build their own paints
- Cutout renders through a canvas layer instead of a full-size scratch bitmap per poster; Split and Brush dispose their gradient shaders
- Letterbox detection scans the pixel buffer directly instead of a native call per pixel
- Bitmap scaling uses explicit cubic resampling now that FilterQuality is gone

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Features
- Generated posters now appear in the episodes Edit Images dialog, so you can pick the frame you want instead of refreshing until you get a good one
- Choose how many alternate posters to offer in Edit Images, from 1 to 10 (default 3)
- Brush style can outline its stroke, sharing the Cutout styles outline toggle
- Element Spacing setting controls the gap between stacked poster elements, so every style spaces them the same way
- The font dropdown now lists the fonts actually installed on your server, and a font that is not installed is called out in the log instead of silently rendering in a substitute face
- Overlay colors collapse to an opacity control when Palette-Derived Colors is on, since the color itself comes from the image

## Breaking
- The scheduled task has been removed. Poster generation now runs entirely as a metadata provider - use a library metadata refresh, or pick a poster from Edit Images
- Processing history and its database have been removed, along with the Reset Processing History button. Jellyfins own refresh options now decide what gets regenerated

## Fixes
- Deleting an episode poster no longer left it permanently blank; there is no tracking state left to say the episode was already done
- Changing a custom font now takes effect; it used to be left out of the change detection entirely
- A tall logo no longer overlaps the episode code beneath it
- Long episode titles wrap to two lines again instead of being shortened to one
- Short titles no longer leave a gap between the episode code and the title
- Cancelling a refresh now stops frame extraction instead of letting it run to completion
- Generated posters are no longer written to the transcode directory and left behind
- Aspect ratios like 2.35:1 now parse correctly on servers with a comma decimal separator
- Saving the Posters tab no longer hangs on a spinner when the save fails, and no longer overwrites the settings on the other tab
- Settings added in a newer version no longer break saving for configurations written by an older one

## Developer
- The frosted panel shape and the brush stroke paths are disposed even when an exception unwinds
- Poster elements are positioned by a shared measure-then-place layout column instead of each style walking its own offsets, and titles are fitted to the height they are given as well as the width
- Poster configuration is never written back during plugin startup, so a failed config load can no longer overwrite good settings with defaults
- Poster rendering returns encoded bytes rather than temp files
- Removed the scheduled task, tracking database, configuration hashing, and around 900 lines of superseded code
- Shaders, mask filters, and image filters are disposed rather than left to finalization; HDR brightening no longer round-trips the whole bitmap through managed memory
- Example templates carry every current setting, and the bundled examples were regenerated
- Test suite grown from 21 to 39 cases, covering layout, title fitting, aspect ratio parsing, font resolution, and the generated image cache
- Bump Base to 2026.7.31

  - Added professional soft shadow blur to all text elements for improved depth and readability
  - Implemented explicit sRGB color space handling for consistent color accuracy across all output formats
  - Increased image encoding quality to 100% for all output formats (JPEG, PNG, WEBP)
  - Enhanced FFmpeg frame extraction quality from q:v 2 to q:v 1 (absolute highest quality)
  - Added RGB24 pixel format specification for better color accuracy during frame extraction
  - Implemented gradient dithering to eliminate color banding in overlay gradients
  - Fixed Frame poster border corners to connect seamlessly without gaps
  - Improved line rendering quality with proper stroke caps across all poster styles

**Fixes**
  
  - Implemented multi-quality frame analysis system combining brightness AND sharpness detection
  - Added Laplacian variance blur detection to reject motion-blurred action shots
  - Created intelligent quality scoring algorithm that weighs both brightness and sharpness
  - Enhanced frame selection logic to find optimal frames instead of just brightest frames
  - HDR-aware quality scoring (60% brightness, 40% sharpness for HDR; 40% brightness, 60% sharpness for SDR)
  - Improved early exit logic for HDR content when quality score exceeds 0.6 threshold
  - Added comprehensive quality metrics logging (brightness, sharpness, and combined score)

**Technical**

  - Added FilterQuality.High to all bitmap drawing operations in CroppingService and poster generators
  - Implemented SubpixelText and LcdRenderText properties for all text paint objects across 6 files
  - Added MaskFilter.CreateBlur(SKBlurStyle.Normal, 1.5f) to all shadow paint objects for soft shadows
  - Configured explicit SKImageInfo with RGBA8888, Premul alpha, and sRGB color space in surface creation
  - Added SKMatrix.Identity to all gradient shader creation for proper dithering support
  - Added IsDither = true to gradient overlay paint for smooth color transitions
  - Implemented StrokeCap.Square and StrokeJoin.Miter to Frame border rendering for precise corner connections
  - Updated Standard separator lines with StrokeCap.Square for cleaner rendering
  - Enhanced Cutout border rendering with StrokeCap.Round and StrokeJoin.Round
  - Added GetFrameSharpness() method using Laplacian operator for edge detection
  - Added CalculateFrameQualityScore() method for combined brightness/sharpness scoring
  - Updated TryExtractionStrategy() to track and compare quality scores instead of brightness alone
  - Modified both SoftwareFFmpegService and HardwareFFmpegService with -q:v 1 -pix_fmt rgb24 parameters

Please find our new examples [here](https://github.com/JPKribs/jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator/tree/master/Examples)!

**Features**
- Added template export/import system for sharing poster configurations
- Export poster configurations as JSON templates with metadata (author, description, & plugin version)
- Import templates from other users to quickly apply custom poster styles

**Documentation**
- Added a page for examples
- Removed old screenshots in favor of examples

**Technical**
- Added TemplateExportService for JSON serialization of poster configurations
- Created PosterTemplate model for shareable configuration format

**Technical:**
* Jellyfin 10.11 Release

**Fixes:**

  - Fixed QSV hardware acceleration failing when tone mapping is disabled
  - Fixed VAAPI, NVENC, and AMF hardware acceleration failing without tone mapping

**Technical:**

  - Changed hwdownload filter to apply unconditionally for all hardware acceleration types
  - Hardware frames now properly convert to CPU format for PNG encoding regardless of tone mapping state

**Fixes:**

  - Fixed QSV hardware acceleration failing with format conversion errors on Linux
  - Fixed QSV tone mapping producing invalid filter chain errors

**Technical:**

  - Changed QSV initialization to use VAAPI as base device matching Jellyfin behavior
  - Changed QSV to use VAAPI hwaccel method instead of direct QSV hwaccel for proper hardware frame handling
  - Changed QSV tone mapping from vpp_qsv to tonemap_vaapi filter for compatibility with VAAPI frame format

### Notice

This version is confirmed on MacOS to resolve SW Tone Mapping and HW Tone Mapping. This being said, I do not have other hardware to test this for QSV, NVENC, and VAAPI but these should mirror how Jellyfin Transcodes work so this _should_ resolve these issues as well.

**Fixes:**

  - Fixed BT.2390 and all tone mapping algorithms failing with Undefined constant error
  - Fixed VideoToolbox hardware acceleration failing to extract frames
  - Fixed QSV hardware tone mapping not working properly
  - Fixed hardware frames not converting to software for PNG encoding

**Technical:**

  - Changed software tone mapping to use tonemapx filter matching Jellyfin transcoding behavior
  - Added VideoToolbox specific tone mapping using scale_vt filter
  - Added QSV specific tone mapping using vpp_qsv filter
  - Added hwdownload filter to convert hardware frames to software for all acceleration types
  - VideoToolbox now always uses hwdownload due to videotoolbox_vld output format
  - Removed unnecessary hardware encoding arguments for PNG output

**Fixes:**

  - Rebuild 10.10.29

**Fixes:**
- Fixed BT.2390 tone mapping failing with Undefined constant error
- Fixed plugin logo not displaying in repository/installed plugins view

**Technical:**
- Corrected tone mapping filter syntax from double tonemap parameter to single in ToneMapFilterService
- Removed GetImage method from Plugin.cs to use Jellyfin default embedded resource mechanism

**Fixes:**
- Fixed duplicate default configurations being created on every plugin initialization/restart
- Fixed saved poster configurations not persisting between restarts
- Fixed UI showing only default configuration until new configuration was created
- Fixed font color and font size controls not hiding for Cutout and Numeral poster styles
- Added validation to prevent saving non-default configurations with no assigned series

**Technical:**
- Changed PluginConfiguration constructor to initialize empty PosterConfigurations list instead of creating default
- Made IsDefault an explicit boolean property instead of computed property based on SeriesIds
- Added automatic default configuration creation in PosterConfigurationService.Initialize() with persistence
- Added null safety checks with error logging in GetSettingsForSeries() and GetSettingsForEpisode()
- Updated configuration loading to properly deserialize from XML without constructor interference

**Other:**

- Added validation to prevent users from naming configurations Default (reserved name)
- Updated UI logic to use IsDefault property instead of index-based detection
- Combined data-depends-on and data-hide-for-styles visibility checks to prevent conflicts

## Notice

### Major Version

The current versioning scheme is Jellyfin-Major.Jellyfin-Minor.Plugin-Version. So, 10.10.1 is Jellyfin 10.10 and version 1 for the plugin. This does a good job of tracking plugin versions and the supported Jellyfin version but it doesnt do a good job of tracking major version changes.

This is a note that this version (10.10.27) is a huge architectural change. You may need to uninstall and reinstall this plugin as the underlying settings for this plugin have changed dramatically to support **series specific posters**!

**This means, you can set a poster per series (or multiple series) or use a single default for all series.**

Cinema Project.description: Every movie already has a soul: most of it buried in a poster and thumbnail. Cinema Project builds a virtual room experience around that instead. Walk through it like a video game: poster art lining the walls, a fanart and video slideshow across the backwall, theme songs filling the room, trailers, theme videos, or the movie itself playing on the screen up front. None of it is new, it's what your library already had, finally given space to be experienced all together, visualized all at once. On top of that, Ambient Mode lets you create your own feature show, similar to a pre-roll.

versions.changelog: Fixes the configuration page on Jellyfin 12, where **nothing worked**. Jellyfin 12 stopped accepting the older of its two ways of proving who you are, and the page was still using it — so every request it made was rejected before it reached the plugin. Libraries did not load, saved templates did not appear, the bundled fonts did not arrive, applying a cover did nothing, and opening the poster browser produced the cryptic message *"Failed to execute 'json' on 'Response': Unexpected end of JSON input"*, which was the rejection with no explanation attached. The page now identifies itself the same way the Jellyfin web client does, which works on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12 alike. **If you installed 4.0.0.0, update** — nothing was wrong with your settings or your covers, the page simply could not reach the server.

**Support for Jellyfin 12.** Jellyfin 12 moved to .NET 10 and changed its plugin ABI, so a plugin built for 10.11 cannot be built for both — this release is built against Jellyfin 12 and requires it. Nothing about designing or rendering covers has changed: your saved templates, applied covers and settings all carry over untouched. If you are **still on Jellyfin 10.11**, stay on **3.5.1.0** — your server will keep being offered that version and will not see this one, so nothing breaks by leaving it alone.

Fixes a small but confusing moment with **Live TV** targets. Live TV has no posters to build a mosaic from, so the **Poster collage** background is unavailable there — and if you had already chosen a collage and then switched the target to Live TV, the background silently changed back to **Image** without a word. The option is now greyed out with a line explaining why, in all three languages, so the change no longer happens behind your back. Nothing else about how covers render has changed.

Adds **Spanish**. The whole configuration page — every step, label, button, hint and message, plus the server's upload and validation errors — is now translated, joining English and Dutch. The page follows your Jellyfin display language, and regional variants come along for the ride: `es-MX` and `es-419` get Spanish just like `es-ES`. Alongside it, the translation files themselves were **cleaned up and put under test**. Roughly a hundred strings left behind by the v3 editor rewrite were still being carried (and would have had to be translated into every new language) — those are gone, and five new build-time checks now fail if a language drifts out of sync with English, if a `{0}` placeholder goes missing, or if a string is defined but never shown. No change to how covers look or render.

Adds an **overlay gradient** to the Background step — a colour that fades in over your background and sits under your text. It is the missing piece behind the look where a poster **resolves into a solid band of colour** at the bottom, with the title on top of it and readable no matter what the poster shows underneath. Each colour stop has its own **opacity**, so you can go from fully transparent to fully solid, use **two colours** for a duotone fade, or wash the whole cover. Four **presets** — Bottom fade, Top fade, Full wash and Duotone — get you there in one click, and switching between them keeps the colours you have already picked so you can try all four without losing your palette. The **Auto palette** swatches now recolour the selected overlay stop, so you can tint a cover with a colour taken straight out of its own artwork. The overlay works with every background type — image, poster collage, gradient or solid — and with animated covers. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.

The configuration page is now a **guided walkthrough**. Instead of every control at once, designing a cover is laid out as five numbered steps — **Target**, **Background**, **Text & logos**, **Effects**, **Output** — with one open at a time and any of them one click away. Each step shows the controls most people need and keeps the rest under **Advanced**. Choosing a background is now a single choice — **image, poster collage, gradient or solid colour** — instead of a source dropdown plus a separate gradient tick that overlapped with it. The whole page is **properly usable on a phone**: bigger touch targets throughout, the preview pinned at the top while you work, a full-screen poster browser, and canvas handles you can actually grab (they used to shrink to a few pixels on a small screen). Two more additions: **undo and redo** across the whole design with Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y, and an **in-context preview** showing your cover wide, square and poster-shaped before you apply it. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.

Adds a new **Effects** card. A **colour wash** tints the background under your text, a **vignette** darkens the edges to draw the eye inward, **film grain** adds texture, and a **border** frames the cover — square or rounded, single or double-lined. Every effect is off until you switch it on, and turning one back down to zero leaves your cover exactly as it was. One click of **Jellyfin style** lays down the familiar dark-gradient look with clean white text, which you can then edit freely. And **Auto palette** reads the dominant colours straight out of your background and offers them as swatches — click one to recolour the selected text layer or the colour wash. Existing designs and saved templates are untouched and render exactly as before.

Covers are no longer one line of text. A new **Layers** card lets you stack **as many text layers as you like** plus your own **PNG logos and icons**, each independently styled and freely placed. Every layer can be **shown or hidden, reordered, duplicated, deleted** and selected from the list, and the card below it edits whichever layer you have selected. On the preview canvas, the selected layer gets **corner handles to resize it** and a **knob to rotate it** — hold **Shift** to keep a logo's proportions or snap rotation to 15°. Two new sliders, **Opacity** and **Rotation**, work on text and logos alike. Logos are uploaded the same way as backgrounds (PNG, transparency preserved) and are restored onto the canvas when you load a saved template. As always the server render stays authoritative, and rotated or faded text now renders there exactly as the preview shows it.

Fixes **Reposition background**, which barely worked in 3.0.0.0. Dragging the background now **follows your cursor exactly** — it used to lag badly at low zoom and overshoot at high zoom, matching the cursor only at one specific zoom level. More importantly, repositioning now **works straight away, without zooming in first**: on a **Fill** background you can slide a portrait poster up and down (or a wide still left and right) to choose which part of it the cover shows. Previously that did nothing at all until you zoomed in, because only the zoomed-in part of the image was treated as movable. The server render and the on-screen canvas were fixed together, so what you position is what gets applied. Designs you have already saved or applied are unaffected and render exactly as before.

The config page preview is now a **live interactive canvas**, not a static image: click the title to select it and **drag it** to position, and toggle **Reposition background** to **drag-pan** and **scroll/pinch-zoom** the background image directly on the canvas. A new **Show server render** button renders the exact same design on the server — the authoritative output, since the canvas is a fast approximation — so you can compare before applying. Designs are now stored internally in a new **layered document format** (title text is one layer, more layer types land in a later release); **existing saved templates migrate automatically** the first time you load them, so nothing is lost.

A code-quality and size pass. The plugin is now **much smaller** — the bundled Noto Sans fonts were subset to the glyphs cover titles use (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, punctuation), cutting the plugin DLL from ~3.9 MB to ~1.6 MB with no visible change. **Dead code was removed** (an unused retry service, an unused exceptions module, and nine internal API endpoints the UI never called), and the render pipeline was tidied up (the image compositing is no longer needlessly async). A few **security hardening** touches: the Apply and batch-apply endpoints are now rate-limited and batch size is capped, text size is clamped, poster-collage sources get the same decompression-bomb guard as other images, and error messages no longer echo server paths back to the browser. Purely internal — no user-facing behaviour changes.

Small UI fixes on the Target card: a **disabled button now clearly looks disabled** (dimmed, not-allowed cursor) — the Restore button no longer looks clickable when there's no backup yet — and the Restore row has proper spacing above it. Also added an animated preview to the README.

The **poster browser now covers every library type** — music albums and artists, books, music videos and photos, not just movies and shows — so you can pick a cover from a music or book library too. A **loading spinner** now shows over the preview while it renders, which helps for slower operations like building a poster collage. The **Apply** button now shows an "Applying…" state and locks while it works, so a slow render (like an animated GIF) no longer looks like nothing is happening. **Animated GIF covers are more reliable**: the working size is capped so a full-size render no longer takes forever or fails to apply, and text scales with it so the look is unchanged. The default **Landscape** size is now a lighter 1280×720 (it was 1920×1080) — plenty for library tiles and much smaller files; 1920 is still available via Custom. And the Templates and collage cards were tidied up — the **Delete** and **Shuffle** buttons now sit neatly next to their dropdowns instead of as oversized blocks.

Polish on the v2 release. The config page now matches Jellyfin more closely — compact colour pickers (they used to stretch the full width), and action buttons that align with the selects beside them. The preview no longer starts on a black canvas: it opens with Jellyfin's **brand gradient** (purple → blue) by default. And uploading an **animated GIF** as a background now animates the preview automatically — it switches to Animated GIF output and passes the source's frames through at their own timing, instead of showing a single still frame.

A big release. **Poster-collage backgrounds** build a grid mosaic from a target's own item posters (with density and shuffle controls). **Design templates** let you save a look and reuse it, and **batch apply** pushes one design onto many libraries, collections or playlists at once — each cover titled with its own target's name. **Animated GIF export** is now real: it passes through an animated-GIF background or applies a Ken Burns pan/zoom (capped at 30 frames). And **Restore original cover** reverts any target to its pre-plugin image — applying a cover now backs up the previous image automatically.

The plugin now has its own entry in the dashboard's left navigation menu, so you no longer have to open it through the Plugins list. Added **Live TV** as a cover target (best-effort — it sets the image on Jellyfin's generated Live TV view, which may not persist on every server). Moved the custom-font picker into the **Text** card where it belongs, and added a screenshot to the README.

Fixed the background dim: any non-zero dimming used to black out a picked poster entirely (JPEG posters have no alpha channel, so the overlay painted fully opaque). Dimming now composites correctly and the default was lowered to 0.25. Added an **Image fit** option — Fill (crop), Fit (show the whole image, letterboxed) or Stretch — so a portrait poster no longer gets cropped to a strip in a wide cover. New **multi-colour gradient** picker with an angle control for linear gradients and add/remove colour stops. You can now target **collections** and **playlists** in addition to libraries.

Poster background reliability: authenticate the image download, build the upload without the (sometimes unavailable) File constructor, and surface a clear message at each step so any failure is visible instead of silent.

Fixes. The config page now reliably follows your Jellyfin UI language — the detection reads Jellyfin's stored language setting, not just the browser language (Dutch now shows correctly). Picking a library poster as the background now works: the image is fetched through Jellyfin's own image endpoint and uploaded, instead of resolving a local file path that wasn't always available.

The config page now follows your Jellyfin UI language, with a complete Dutch (NL) translation and English fallback. Font weight now works — all six weights (Light–ExtraBold) are bundled as distinct Noto Sans faces. Background images are cover-fitted instead of stretched, so posters keep their aspect ratio. Added a Landscape 16:9 preset (now the default, best for library covers), a Download button for the generated image, and logging when a background image can't be used.

Redesigned the config page into a native Jellyfin two-column layout with grouped cards and a sticky **live preview** that updates automatically as you adjust settings (no more manual preview button). Styled the file pickers as native buttons showing the chosen file, and made allowed formats and size limits explicit. Fixed the empty library dropdown (libraries now come from GetVirtualFolders). Backfilled earlier version changelogs.

Bundled Noto Sans so titles always render (even on Docker/minimal Linux). Security & correctness hardening: fixed path-traversal and decompression-bomb risks, added rate limiting and font-signature validation, safe colour parsing, image disposal, and generated-file cleanup.
Initial release: custom library cover art with text, gradients, blur, custom backgrounds and fonts, a live preview, and a picker for existing library posters.

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10
Fix 3.2 build issues.

## Developer
- Server routes moved under the Allow system access toggle, so a page needs one permission instead of two
- Shortened the configuration page help text

## Features
- Allow local resource calls, so a page can define named server side routes and call them with serverFetch while the server forwards each to its configured target
- Optional per page Allow system access toggle that runs a page without the sandbox, so its scripts can call the Jellyfin API and reach other resources on this origin
- Pages on a signed in tier can now be restricted to named users, defaulting to all users at that tier

## Developer
- Defining a route also runs its page unsandboxed, since the helper cannot reach the route from an opaque origin
- A route credential stored before encryption existed is upgraded on the next save rather than left in the clear
- Route credentials are encrypted at rest and never sent to a browser, and the configuration page posts back a sentinel so an untouched field keeps the stored value
- Forwarded requests carry the caller's headers minus a deny list, so the viewer's Jellyfin session is never handed to a route target
- Route targets must be absolute http or https URLs fixed in configuration, so a page cannot turn a route into an open proxy
- A restricted page is refused before its body is rendered, so content never reaches a viewer the list does not name
- An allow list is refused on an anonymous page at save time, and fails closed at serve time if the stored list is unusable
- Pages stay sandboxed by default, and an unsandboxed page still reaches the browser HTML encoded inside the wrapper's srcdoc
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Developer
- Serve every page under one Content-Security-Policy so a page behaves the same at any visibility tier
- Allow pages to load external resources and submit forms, which the anonymous tier previously blocked
- Allow pages to be embedded by the Jellyfin origin (frame-ancestors 'self')
- Serve page HTML as UTF-8 so single-file documents without a charset meta tag render correctly
- Sign in correctly when the web client is signed in to more than one server
- Reject unknown visibility tiers and malformed asset content types when configuration is saved
- Key the decoded asset cache to the asset itself, closing a stale-bytes window around a save
- Keep unsaved page edits when switching pages in the dashboard
- Declare targetAbi 10.11.10.0 to match the Jellyfin packages the plugin is compiled against

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a dns icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Fixed
- The plain-http warning no longer logs the request URL's authority, which carried the update secret into the server log for providers whose credential lives in the URL's userinfo (ClouDNS DynURL, Directnic gateway URL). The warning now names the record's hostname instead
- A Data Protection key store that fails for an unexpected reason surfaces instead of being silently downgraded to plaintext credential storage; the expected failures (bad path, no permission, no service) still fall back as before

## Developer
- Address the outstanding CodeQL findings across the plugin and test projects (LINQ filtering and projection, ternary assignment, dictionary lookup, response disposal in the HTTP test stub)

## Fixed
- Resolve the TTL "1 = automatic" sentinel to a per-provider default instead of sending a literal one-second TTL (Gandi, GoDaddy, Spaceship, Hetzner, DNSExit)
- Yandex matches records by type as well as name, so an IPv4 update can no longer overwrite an AAAA or TXT record, and A/AAAA now update independently
- Spaceship writes the new record before removing stale ones, so a failed update leaves the old address serving instead of deleting the record
- Hetzner treats an accepted, still-applying action as success instead of timing out and counting a false failure toward backoff
- DNS Made Easy treats "no update required" as success instead of walking a healthy record into backoff
- DDNS.fm validates the response body instead of treating any HTTP 200 as success
- NS1 record creation sends the required zone, domain, and type fields, so first-time setup works
- Apex hostnames infer the correct domain when no zone is set (Porkbun, Dynadot, Spaceship, Dinahosting), and Dinahosting gained an optional Zone field
- OVH DynHost, DynDNS v1, DSLReports, and NearlyFreeSpeech.NET declare IPv4-only, so an IPv6 address is no longer recorded as pushed and endlessly re-pushed
- A record with one working address family is no longer paused by backoff when only the other family fails

## Developer
- Harden the publish workflow (release body via env, tag-derived version, fail-fast asset downloads, required tag on manual dispatch)
- Slash-command dispatch uses the JF_BOT_TOKEN secret instead of a placeholder
- CI packages with build.sh and verifies the zip contents, and build.sh parses build.yaml colon- and space-safely
- Response-parsing tests for every provider plus orchestrator and API tests

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12
- Use ActivityLogger from Base 2026.7.12
- Use BackoffPolicy from Base 2026.7.12

## Feature
- Output logging to Activity Logs for better visibility

## Security
- Encrypt credentials saved through the generic plugin configuration endpoint instead of waiting for the next run
- Warn in the log when a record updates over plain http
- Show a dashboard warning when credential encryption is unavailable and secrets are stored in plaintext

## Developer
- Share one SecretProtector between the dashboard and generic save paths
- Snapshot the configuration per update run instead of mutating live records

## Fixes
- Prune record status against fresh record ids so a record added mid-run is not dropped

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.6.23
- Fix encryption of tokens to ensure they will not break between versions
- Migrate everything so it lives in the provider for ease of maintenance
- Reorganize files

## Documentation
- Creates Provider documentation per ddclient

## Fixes
- Check the DNS for current IP instead of always resending
- If the current DNS is internal, use the previous IP sent (previous behavior)

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.6.19
- Fix encryption of tokens to ensure they will not break between versions

## Fixes
- Remove URL from logging

## Initial release

This plugin acts as a DDNS resolver using Jellyfin as its host. A lot of this work will look very similar to [ddclient](https://github.com/ddclient/ddclient) which was a huge help and inspiration for this plugin. This takes the work they've taken and wraps it into a Jellyfin plugin for server owners don't want to manage more than one application.

versions.changelog: # 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

Hero Bar.description: A from-scratch, in-flow rotating featured-content hero for the Jellyfin home page, built as a lighter-weight, fully compatible replacement for the third-party Media Bar plugin. Inserted as a normal first child of the home tab content (not a body-level overlay), so it never overlaps or requires manual positioning fixes against other home rows. Mixes recently added items with a trending row, shows ClearLogo art with a text-title fallback, rating/year/genre metadata, overview, and Play/Info/Favorite buttons with clickable pagination dots.

versions.changelog:
Afspil-knappen følger temaets egne farver - på ElegantFin lysegrå med sort tekst - i stedet for Jellyfins blå, også mens temaet indlæses.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Forsiden hentes meget hurtigere.

- Alle otte baggrunde blev hentet på én gang i 1920 gange skærmens pixeltæthed - 2880 px på en almindelig bærbar og 3,5 MB, mens forsiden stadig var ved at indlæse. Nu hentes kun det slide, der vises, og det næste, i en størrelse der passer til skærmen.
- Logoerne hentes også først, når deres slide er på vej.
- Indtil baggrunden er hentet, vises en sløret udgave af den.
- Størrelserne er dem, New Badges 2.8.2.0 laver på forhånd på serveren, så billederne kommer med det samme.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Intet blink i topbaren, når du scroller helt op.

- Når siden ramte toppen, skiftede Jellyfin 12 topbarens udseende og fjernede samtidig den markering, der gør den gennemsigtig over banneret. I et splitsekund kom temaets farvede bar frem og forsvandt igen. Markeringen sidder nu et sted, Jellyfin ikke rører, så topbaren forbliver gennemsigtig.
- Topbaren bliver nu gennemsigtig med det samme i stedet for at tone ud, så temaets farve ikke hænger et øjeblik i toppen, når du hopper helt op.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Mindre prikker på mobil og tablet.

- Prikkerne, der viser hvilket slide du er på, fyldte omkring halvdelen af skærmbredden på en telefon. De er nu mindre og tættere.
- Den aktive prik blev tegnet i hele sit trykfelt og var derfor en stor hvid plet. Den er nu kun lidt større end de andre.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Ingen streg under den gennemsigtige topbar.

- Skyggen, der holder topbarens knapper læsbare over banneret, sad på selve topbaren og stoppede ved dens underkant, så den tegnede omridset af den gamle topbar. Den ligger nu på banneret og toner blødt ud et godt stykke længere nede.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Gennemsigtig topbar over banneret på Jellyfin 12.

- Banneret går helt op under topbaren, og topbaren er gennemsigtig, så billedet fylder hele toppen af forsiden.
- Når du scroller forbi banneret, bliver topbaren almindelig igen.
- På Favoritter, Tilføj, Kalender og alle andre sider er topbaren som før.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- Banneret husker sine slides mellem besøg - de skifter alligevel kun hver 48. time - så det vises med det samme, når du åbner appen. Før blev 400 titler hentet igen ved hvert besøg, mens Jellyfins egne rækker ventede.
- Når der skal vælges nye slides, hentes kun id'erne på de 400 kandidater og derefter de 8 valgte, i stedet for alle detaljer om alle 400.
- Afspil/Fortsæt og favorit-hjertet opdateres, når Jellyfins egne rækker er indlæst, så banneret ikke sinker dem.
- Scriptet caches af browseren og hentes kun igen, når plugin'et er opdateret.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Indstillingssiden er tegnet om, så den ser ud som resten af Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 har lavet sine egne indstillingssider om: felterne er nu fyldte bokse med en lille etiket øverst i selve feltet, i stedet for en label ovenover. Denne side fulgte stadig den gamle stil og stak derfor ud fra alt andet i dashboardet.

Felter, afkrydsningsfelter, overskrifter og Gem-knappen matcher nu Jellyfin 12's egne — samme højde, samme afrunding, samme farver. Farverne hentes fra Jellyfin 12's eget tema, så siden også følger med hvis du skifter tema.

Kun udseende. Der er ikke ændret noget i hvad siden gør, eller i indstillingerne selv. På Jellyfin 10.11 ser siden ud præcis som før — den nye stil slås kun til, hvis serveren rent faktisk er 12.

Retter at pluginets indstillingsside ikke kunne åbnes på Jellyfin 12.

Pluginet kørte fint, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun en plugin-indstillingsside, hvis siden selv beder om at komme i menuen. Det gør den nu.

Kun relevant for Jellyfin 12 — på 10.11 kunne siden altid åbnes fra plugin-oversigten uanset hvad.

Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12. Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan KUN installeres der - Jellyfin 10.11 bliver på 2.0.4.0, som stadig virker uændret. Serveren vælger selv den rigtige.

Hvad der skulle laves om: Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende adgangsnøglen på (X-Emby-Token), så alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt i stedet. Uden det svarede serveren 401, og heroens "mest sete"-data kunne ikke hentes.

Accentfarven læses nu direkte fra temaet. Før blev den gættet ved at male en usynlig knap med Jellyfins egne klasser og aflæse farven - men Jellyfin 12 tegner sine knapper på en helt ny måde, hvor den klasse ikke findes, så gættet slog fejl og faldt tilbage til en fast farve. Jellyfin 12 udstiller hele sin farvepalet direkte, så nu bliver den bare spurgt. På 10.11 fungerer den gamle metode som før.

Rettet: Afspil/Fortsæt-knappen i hero-baren skiftede af og til til Jellyfins standardblå i stedet for temaets egen grå. Pluginet aflæser temaets accentfarve fra siden, og hvis den aflæsning sker før temaets stylesheet er nået at blive indlæst – på denne server hentes skinnet via et @import fra et CDN – aflæses browserens standardfarve i stedet, og så faldt knappen tilbage til blå. Farven blev kun genberegnet ved DOM-ændringer (højst hvert 10. sekund), så på en side der lå stille kunne den blive blå indtil næste genindlæsning. Nu huskes den sidst korrekt aflæste farve, så en mislykket aflæsning aldrig kan overskrive en god, og farven genberegnes desuden et par gange kort efter sideindlæsning og igen ved "load".

Mindre mørklægning af billedet i hero-baren. Toningen bag titel og knapper er sat ned til 70% af det oprindelige, og ind-/udtoningen i top og bund er trukket ind (18%/78% → 10%/86%), så en større del af plakaten er synlig. Styrken kan nu justeres i indstillingerne ("Artwork tint strength") mellem 0 og 150% – teksten har sin egen skygge, så den kan læses et godt stykke under 100.

Hero-baren kan nu vise et tilfældigt udvalg fra hele biblioteket i stedet for "trending + senest tilføjet" - og udvalget er det SAMME for alle brugere på serveren. Det skiftes automatisk ud hver 48. time (kan ændres i indstillingerne). Udvalget trækkes ikke tilfældigt pr. bruger eller pr. sideindlæsning - det udledes af uret, så alle lander på præcis de samme titler uden at serveren skal gemme noget, og det skifter helt af sig selv når vinduet ruller over (justeret efter UTC, så det sker samtidigt for alle). Kan slås fra igen i indstillingerne.

Rettelse på mobil: slide-prikkerne lå oven i knapperne. Prikkerne sad nederst til højre - samme linje som Afspil/Info/Favorit-rækken - og blev tegnet ovenpå den. Målt live på en 360px skærm med dansk knaptekst (Fortsæt i stedet for Afspil) overlappede de to 112 pixels, så prikkerne løb tværs hen over Info- og favoritknappen. Det er et pladsproblem, som først opstår omkring 470px, og derfor kun ses på telefon: knapraden mod otte berøringsvenlige prikker klemt op i højre side. På skærme under 500px flytter prikkerne nu op i øverste højre hjørne - fri plads i alle slides, eftersom motivet ligger i midten/til højre og teksten nederst til venstre, og netop dér en karrusel normalt viser sin position på mobil.

Bygget til at kunne deles. Farvetonen hen over billedet og knapperne henter nu deres farver fra det tema du kører, i stedet for at være håndmatchet til ét bestemt skin, så heroen glider ind i et hvilket som helst tema - også de lyse. Knapteksterne følger Jellyfins egen sprogindstilling (dansk/engelsk, eller tvunget). Nye indstillinger: sprog, højde, om synopsis og favoritknappen skal vises, og hvor langt tilbage trending kigger.

Ens knapform i alle vinduesstørrelser. Info/Afspil/Favorit-knapperne har nu præcis samme facon i fuldskærm, halvt vindue og på mobil: fast min-højde + border-box ligger i grundreglen, og media queries ændrer ikke længere padding/højde (det var dem der gjorde knapperne synligt anderledes ved smallere bredder).

Fixes the Info button looking visibly 'fluffier' than the Play/Favorite buttons next to it: Info is an <a> element while the other two are real <button>s, and without an explicit reset each rendered with its own element's default font/appearance despite sharing the same CSS class. Added a font-family/line-height/appearance reset to the shared button style so all three render pixel-consistent.

Mobile + performance: touch swipe changes hero slides, with touch events contained inside the hero so Jellyfin's tab strip no longer hijacks a hero swipe into a tab switch (the swipe-to-Favoritter bug); vertical scrolling unaffected. Manual slide changes (dots, swipes) share the rotation's slide counter and restart its timer, fixing desynced auto-flips. Tailored phone layout: shorter banner, tighter text/logo sizing, tappable 40px buttons, larger dot hit areas. Performance: recently-added/trending pool cached 10 min in sessionStorage so the hero paints instantly on revisit; resume/next-up state always fetched fresh.

Visual: the hero now blends into the page background instead of ending in a hard box edge. The backdrop and tint layers sit behind a vertical alpha mask that fades them out at the top and bottom, letting ElegantFin's real background gradient (measured live: linear-gradient(0deg, rgb(28,30,34) 35%, rgb(37,39,45))) show through - a true blend with no color matching involved. Text, buttons, and pagination dots are outside the masked layer and stay fully crisp.

Fix: v1.0.0.0 could stack many duplicate heroes on the home page - the duplicate check ran synchronously but insertion happened after async data fetches, so every DOM mutation during that window started another insert; now guarded by a synchronously-set pending flag plus a re-check right before insertion. Play button now actually starts playback (remote-controls the client's own session via the Sessions PlayNow command) instead of linking to the details page, with details as fallback if the play command fails. Dynamic play button: shows Fortsæt and resumes where you left off for partially-watched movies, and for series in progress plays the half-watched episode (Resume) or the next unwatched episode (NextUp).

Initial release. Recently added + trending item mix (trending via the same Playback Reporting query New Badges' Trending row uses), ClearLogo image per slide with automatic text-title fallback when no logo art exists, rating/year/age-rating/genre metadata line, truncated overview, Play/Info/Favorite buttons, clickable pagination dots, and configurable slide count/rotation interval/trending toggle. Built as an in-flow first child of #homeTab (not a body-level overlay like Media Bar), so it never overlaps Mine medier/Continue Watching and needs no manual positioning fixes. Uses the verified ElegantFin header color (rgba(30,40,54,...)) for its gradient overlay so it blends into the header with no seam at any window width.

Pick the columns you want per media type.

versions.changelog:
### Added

- A Quality column that names the class a frame falls in, from 144p to 8K, with an i in place of the p for interlaced video. It sorts by class rather than by how the name reads, and a filter picks a class from a list and holds rows at, above or below it. (#7)
- `Schema` answers the classes a quality can be held against, in their order.
- A failed export and a failed column save are reported in words of their own.

### Changed

- A CSV names the unit of a size, a runtime and a bitrate in its header. An ODS shows a runtime as a time, counted in hours past a day, and a size and a bitrate with their unit, all of them still numbers a spreadsheet can total. (#6)
- A number typed into a filter with the digit grouping the table prints is read as one number, so 48,000 is no longer 48.
- The README describes `search` and what an export holds, and names bytes per hour and truth values among the filter values.
- An advisory against a package Jellyfin brings along is a build warning rather than an error.

### Fixed

- The sidebar entry followed a language further down the browser's list when English came first, and could take one the browser had ruled out.
- A book ran for the second Jellyfin measures its reading progress in, and was given a size per hour from it.
- A series whose episodes run at 24000/1001 and at 2997/125 read as mixed in its frame rate, though every episode shows 23.976.
- A DVD or Blu-ray folder weighed only the first file of its title. It now weighs every file in the folder and shows no size per hour.
- A .strm took its bitrate and its size per hour from the bytes of the text file.
- The table kept its scroll position when a page turn, a sort, a search or a filter replaced its rows.
- A visit whose schema failed to load left an empty page behind, and a later one left the filter button disabled.
- Two quick changes to the rows per page or to the level a tab is expanded to could be stored in the wrong order.
- The spacing of the tab counts, the column picker and the row toggles did not follow a right-to-left layout.
- Three checks could not fail or skipped part of what they name: the rounded runtime of a series, the version in the README badge, and the names of the tabs.
- A failed library refresh ended the test run, a request the server never answered held it for good, and Ctrl-C waited for the helper container to finish.
- The fixture recipe of the screenshot script went on after a failed encode, and the version list did not retry a connection that dropped after the request was sent.

### Dependencies

- jsdom 30.1.1 in the tests. (#4)
- Renovate keeps `test/` in its scan through an empty `ignorePaths` rather than `ignorePresets`.

### Added

- Conditions on any column, up to twenty per request: at least, at most, equals, differs from, contains, does not contain, is empty and is not empty, whichever of them fit the column. A value is typed in the unit the table shows, a filtered tab lists the level it is expanded to, flat, and an export writes exactly those rows.
- Inventory has its own entry in the dashboard sidebar, worded in the language the browser asks in.
- The table opens on the Inventory logo, worded in the language the page is in and linking to the project.
- Music filed loose beside the albums is listed with them, since no row opens to reach it.
- The plugin archive carries its image, so the catalog and the plugins page show the logo rather than an empty tile.
- `Schema` answers the conditions each column can be held against and how many of them one request may carry.

### Changed

- The Music tab counts tracks rather than albums, and is called Music rather than Albums.
- The table fills the window, with its header held in place while the rows scroll.
- Plays and Plays (all users) read 0 rather than an empty cell, so a condition and a sort can hold them.
- Size, duration and bitrate are held against a range rather than an exact value, which a column shown rounded to a unit could never meet.
- A number is typed with a decimal comma where the language uses one, and a value that cannot be read is marked rather than quietly dropped.
- Leaving the page and coming back finds the tab the way it was left, with its sort and its page.
- Every text cell of a CSV is quoted once it holds a separator, whichever one the file itself uses.
- A film or episode kept in several cuts, any of them split into parts, reports the bytes of every file. It and the folders above it show no size per hour, and its bitrate is that of the cut being served.
- A manual install is described by the plugins folder of the server's data directory, rather than by the Docker path alone.
- Bug reports ask for the steps, a screenshot and the log lines; a pull request agrees to the contributor license agreement by checkbox, which a workflow checks.

### Fixed

- A filtered table of fewer than five rows collapsed to nothing on a low window.
- A film grouped with a version in another library was weighed twice on Jellyfin 12.1.
- A film played in its second cut showed no play count and no date, though Jellyfin counts it played.
- Firefox showed rows above the table header after a wheel scroll.
- A second address for the page bound its controls to the view the web client had kept, leaving the new one empty.
- A page turned inside the pause after typing a condition left the table behind the end of what it lists.
- A page left behind by a library that shrank falls back to the last page there is.
- A condition on a column a plugin update no longer offers took the whole page down, on that visit and every later one.
- The page stops offering conditions once the server would refuse another.
- Exports in Arabic and Persian wrote a decimal separator no spreadsheet reads.
- A download the browser gave up on is no longer logged as a server error.
- A failed request no longer leaves another tab's rows on screen or skips the page, sort and total that are drawn, and the column picker no longer stores a selection for a level that is not shown.
- An expanded row closes again when the table it was opened in is replaced, and expansion requests left over from another tab are no longer sent.
- A numeric first column is no longer right-aligned where rows expand, which hid their indentation, and height is printed without digit grouping.
- The API rejects `parentIds` as soon as one id is not a guid.
- The first build of a table asks which library a folder belongs to once rather than once per item in it.

### Security

- A name holding a semicolon or a tab could start a formula in a spreadsheet set to split there, since only the separator of the file itself was quoted.
- An invented culture name on an export answered with an error and grew a cache that is never freed, and a lone surrogate in a condition answered with an error as well. Both are refused now.
- A configuration saved through Jellyfin's own endpoint with empty lists made every endpoint of the plugin fail until the next restart.

### Dependencies

- Renovate follows the Node, jsdom and Playwright versions the tests are pinned to, alongside the GitHub Actions and the analyzers it already tracked.

### Added

- Rows per page, chosen in the footer and kept across restarts, from 50 up to 10000.
- Three columns totalling playback over every account on the server: how often something was played, when it last was, and how many accounts have played it to the end, which on a folder counts only the accounts that have played everything below it.
- The tab whose rows are on their way and the export being built now show that they are working.
- `Schema` reports the culture it answered in, which is what the page takes its plural form from.

### Changed

- What was labelled Played is now Fully played, since Jellyfin only ticks it when something ran to the end.
- The export is written to a temporary file rather than built in memory, and stops when the browser goes away.
- `Items` and `Export` refuse a sort column they do not know instead of quietly sorting by the first one.
- Every change is tested against each Jellyfin release from 12.0 on, one run per major and minor version, taken from the published image tags.

### Fixed

- A film split across several files reported the size of the first file alone, and no runtime at all.
- A trailer or a making of sitting beside a film was listed as an item of its own, in a tab of its own, and its bytes counted towards the totals.
- The frame rate could read 1000 fps where Jellyfin's own interface shows the real one.
- An item Jellyfin marks played on reaching the end of playback did not reach the table until the next stop report.
- The two dropdowns had no arrow, the search field put an empty label into the toolbar, and a disabled button looked exactly like one that could be clicked.
- A first load that failed left the page blank, with an empty column picker behind the Columns button.
- Expanding a level asked for every fifty rows at once, so a large page could open hundreds of requests at a time.
- A row that turned out to have nothing below it lost its control, its alignment with the rows around it, and the keyboard focus.
- A long path was never shortened, and the footer could not wrap in a narrow window.
- The page indicator is announced when it changes, and the control that opens a row says which row it opens.

### Dependencies

- The release archive is uploaded with the gh CLI; softprops/action-gh-release is no longer used.

### Added

- One table in the dashboard listing everything in the libraries, from a whole series down to a single episode, with 38 columns across General, Video, Audio, Subtitles and Playback.
- Folder rows total what is below them: size, runtime and item count add up, an attribute the children disagree on reads as Mixed, and playback folds from the episodes or tracks underneath.
- A column selection per level and how far a tab opens, both remembered across restarts.
- Search across every level of a tab, sorting on any column, and paging.
- Export of the current view as CSV or ODS, in the language of the interface.
- English, German, Spanish, French and Italian.

JellyTrend.description: Syncs TMDB trending movies & TV shows with your local library and provides a Netflix-style banner carousel on the home screen.
JellyTrend.overview: JellyTrend empareja contenido en tendencia de TMDB con tu biblioteca Jellyfin usando provider IDs, genera recomendaciones personalizadas por usuario y lo muestra en un carrusel de banners y en canales para todos los clientes.

versions.changelog:
3.0.0 - El plugin pasa a aprender el gusto de cada usuario

Refactor casi completo desde la 2.0.4: la lista de tendencias de TMDB deja de ser el centro y el perfil de cada usuario pasa a serlo. Requiere .NET 10.

Novedades
- Motor de recomendaciones por usuario: afinidades (generos, decadas, personas, valoraciones, duracion) aprendidas del consumo real, y puntuacion de cada titulo de la biblioteca contra ese perfil.
- Arranque en frio: mientras un usuario no alcanza el minimo de titulos vistos (configurable), su fila se arma con lo que ve el resto del servidor.
- Reserva y rotacion: la lista guardada es mas larga que la fila visible y va cambiando de punto de partida cada cierto tiempo.
- Reparto series/peliculas en la lista de Trendings, con relleno para que la fila nunca quede corta.
- Items de canal materializados para todos los usuarios (ya no dependen de que alguien abra el canal) y cache por usuario en los dos canales, sin fugas entre usuarios.
- El perfil se refresca con los eventos de reproduccion, sin esperar a la corrida programada.
- Panel nuevo de cuatro pestanas (Trendings, Recomendaciones, Almacenamiento y Actividad), con icono propio en la barra lateral, textos en espanol e ingles, estado real del almacenamiento e historial de cada corrida.
- Almacen opcional en PostgreSQL: con el PostgreSQL Database Provider los datos viven en el esquema jellytrend con historial, y las recomendaciones pasan a SQL nativo optimizado (4-10x). Los JSON de la carpeta de datos quedan como copia de cortesia.
- README en espanol (por defecto) y en ingles, con capturas de las cuatro pestanas, el carrusel y los dos canales.

Compatibilidad
- Jellyfin 12.1.x - .NET 10.
- Para Jellyfin 10.11.x usa la version 2.0.4.

Novedades en v2.0.4:

- Integracion opcional con PostgreSQL: si usas Jellyfin Database Providers PostgreSQL, el motor de recomendaciones usa SQL nativo optimizado (4-10x mas rapido en bibliotecas grandes). La integracion se activa sola al detectar el plugin.
- Fix: recomendaciones ya no incluyen contenido visto al momento del sync semanal (excluye played + in-progress en la generacion del JSON).
- Fix: canal Trendings filtra peliculas ya vistas por usuario en tiempo real.
- Fix: canal Recomendados baraja el orden por usuario/hora para mostrar titulos distintos en cada visita al home.
- Fix: banner corregido error 401 con interceptor XHR; el carousel se renderiza una sola vez y cesa el polling innecesario.

Fix en v2.0.3:

- Fix: el banner del carousel ahora se carga correctamente en todas las instalaciones. El script se inyecta directamente en index.html al iniciar el servidor, en lugar de depender del pipeline de peticiones HTTP que no estaba disponible para plugins cargados dinamicamente.
- Fix: acceder a la URL raiz del servidor con el banner activo ya no rompe la carga del cliente web (error 404 en assets JavaScript y CSS).
- Fix: el logger del plugin ahora escribe correctamente desde el primer arranque sin depender de librerias externas.

Correcciones y mejoras en v2.0.2:

- Fix: sombras de películas en Recomendaciones — metadatos, imágenes locales y estado visto sincronizados con la biblioteca.
- Fix: sombras de series en Trendings — temporadas reproducibles e imágenes locales; jamás episodios en la fila.
- Fix: banner móvil — swipe horizontal corregido y paginación por contador en móvil.
- Nueva función: seleccionar si se muestran series en Trendings (aplica al canal, la fila del home y el banner).
- Sync de sombras optimizado (solo persiste cambios) y logger propio mensual.

Correcciones:
- Canal «Recomendados» vacío en la fila de inicio: Jellyfin refrescaba la fila con un usuario vacío y el canal no encontraba las recomendaciones. Ahora el canal resuelve al usuario autenticado a partir del token de la petición y envía sus recomendaciones reales.
- Logs: ruido reducido a nivel Debug y eliminadas las líneas con el id de usuario crudo.
- Banner móvil: hero con altura proporcional a la pantalla, sinopsis visible (2 líneas), botones compactos y paginación reposicionada.
Lanzamiento 2.0.0: plantilla oficial, recomendaciones personalizadas por usuario, navegación por temporadas en los canales, banner por usuario y publicación en GitHub.
