versions.changelog:
v3.0.0.4 - Per-library file counts, boxset link fix

- The Per-Library Breakdown now shows a file count below every size value (trickplay folders included), so sparse and dense libraries are distinguishable at a glance
- Boxset library rows no longer link into the Library Explorer, whose scope excludes boxsets; they render as plain text instead of opening an empty state
- Every task dropdown in Settings now explains what the task does, via an info button next to each task name, in all dashboard languages
- The Overview Trickplay card now also shows the space used by trickplay images Jellyfin stores internally, on its own line below the alongside-media total, marked with an (internal) badge, or as the headline when no alongside data exists
- Compact log view on phones: log entries stack as cards below 700 px instead of squeezing into a four-column table, so no horizontal scrolling is needed, and rows keep breathing room at the screen edges
- Roomier Library Explorer filter popovers on phones using nearly the full viewport width, like the bitrate editor
- Tested by 6219 unit tests and 352 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.3 - Library Explorer, new Codecs breakdowns, disabled users ignored

- The Codecs tab now has a Library Explorer: combine resolution, codecs, bitrate, languages, watched users and formats into one search, scoped to the libraries you pick in its multi-select, so you can find e.g. all 4K films with low bitrate
- Options with zero matches under the other filters are hidden automatically, dimensions without matches stay greyed out, and multi-value dropdowns accept several audio languages, subtitle languages or users at once
- Every active filter is shown in the result header and a Reset button clears the whole search; results arrive as the familiar grouped file tree with Movies, TV Shows and other sections
- Jump straight into the search from the Overview: each library name and all four media cards open the Explorer pre-filtered to that scope
- Every categorical filter can be negated with Includes/Excludes, so you can search e.g. audio languages that are not German; excluded picks show as ≠ pills and counts preview what stays
- Four new breakdowns in the Codecs tab, each with drill-down to the exact files: Video Bitrate (7 tiers from < 2 to > 60 Mbps), Audio Languages, Subtitle Languages and Watched (by username plus Never watched)
- Each bitrate tier uses what Jellyfin measured for the video stream; when a file has no per-stream value the average is estimated from its size and runtime, so almost every file lands in a real tier instead of Unknown
- Disabled Jellyfin users no longer skew results: their old plays are excluded from Smart Recommendations, watch history and the new Watched breakdown
- Long breakdowns start collapsed behind a Show-all toggle with Unknown always last, and unreadable language tags fold into Unknown instead of junk entries
- Added responsive, independently scrollable library result cards.
- Improved compact layouts for mobile controls.
- Added consistent themed scrollbar styling across plugin panels and lists.
- The Overview Per-Library Breakdown has a new Other column per library covering NFO files, text files and other unrecognized sidecar files, plus a Books column whenever a book library exists, so every row adds up exactly to its Total
- Tested by 6169 unit tests and 341 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.2 - Log tab, save bar, resolution and touch fixes

- Clearing the plugin log no longer briefly shows a false "Failed to clear logs." error: the Clear button now confirms success immediately and refreshes the view right away
- Genuine clear failures (e.g. expired session or server error) now write a structured diagnostic to the browser console with the HTTP status and error kind, alongside the visible red button feedback, so a real problem is never silent
- Save bar no longer crowds on phones: the unsaved-changes label and Save button now stack on narrow screens, so long translations like the German "Nicht gespeichert" are no longer cut off
- Widescreen films are counted at their real resolution: cinemascope masters like 1920x800 or 1920x1040 are now correctly shown as 1080p instead of 720p in the Codecs tab, decided by whichever axis reaches a resolution class
- The resolution drill-down now lists each file's exact pixel dimensions (e.g. 1920x800) next to its name, readable on desktop and phones
- Chart tooltips work reliably on touch: the first tap on the Trends chart or a Codecs ring now shows and keeps the tooltip instead of flashing it away, and a second tap on the same Codecs segment closes it
- The save confirmation only appears after a real save: reverting a setting back to its original value no longer briefly shows "All changes saved"
- Tested by 5535 unit tests and 320 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.1 - Per-instance library allocation for Arr

- Assign specific Jellyfin libraries to each Radarr/Sonarr instance, so the Arr tab compares an instance only against the libraries it manages
- With two or more instances of a type, each gets a picker in Settings listing only the matching kind of library (movies for Radarr, TV for Sonarr)
- Leave a picker empty to keep it automatic: instances are matched to libraries from their root folders
- Assignments are kept across backup and restore
- Fixes a 4K instance flagging every 1080p film as "not in Radarr"
- Tested by 5499 unit tests and 318 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.0 - Major release for Jellyfin 12.0+

- Books in your library overview: eBook libraries now show their size and file count on the Overview tab and count towards your storage totals, and they're always protected from every cleanup task
- Smarter recommendations: a much bigger model, fairer suggestions for brand-new users, and more variety in your top picks (no more ten near-identical films in a row)
- Recommendations now also learn from franchises/collections, country of origin, collection & folder themes, whether a series is finished or ongoing, writers/creators, top-billed cast, and how rare a genre or studio is in your library (each signal is optional per item, so missing metadata never skews a pick)
- Fresh picks appear between nightly runs, and faster generation on big libraries
- Redesigned Settings, Health and Arr tabs with a live 'reachable' indicator, plus a sticky save bar and unsaved-changes warning
- Better on phones
- Stronger security: API keys are never shown to the browser, backups can leave keys out, and cleanup can never delete or touch anything outside your media libraries
- Safer trash and cleanup: turning retention off really turns it off, trashing a shortcut never removes the file it points to, and Windows shortcut handling is fixed
- More accurate library stats and safer Seerr request cleanup
- More reliable saves and backups (no more rare 'lost save' when antivirus is scanning)
- New end-to-end test suite runs the plugin inside a real Jellyfin 12 server on every change and proves cleanup stays inside your libraries
- Note: your recommendation model retrains from scratch after upgrading, so suggestions settle back in over the next scheduled runs
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v2.1.0.6: Diagnostics for reverse-proxy / WAF-blocked config saves. Added GET /JellyfinHelper/Ping liveness endpoint. Configuration model-binding and validation errors are now logged to the plugin log (source "API", level WARN) instead of silently returning 400. Frontend save handler now classifies errors (network / proxy / server / unauthorized) and surfaces the HTTP status and body snippet to the console, with an automatic Ping follow-up to distinguish "backend unreachable" from "backend reachable, payload rejected". 2325 tests.

v2.1.0.5: Fix StackOverflow on circular symlinks in directory scan. Fix IOException on long trash path names. Added Swedish (sv) language. Exclude Libraries multi-select dropdown. Trash folder browser. Trash path change dialog (move/delete content on path change). Enhanced trash path validation. Upgraded to Jellyfin 10.11.10. 2318 tests.
v2.1.0.4: Fix MissingMethodException for IUserManager.Users.

v2.1.0.3: Add TMDB and Seerr deep links on discovery card flip-back (opens system browser on mobile). Fix 400 Bad Request when submitting discovery requests on Seerr instances with 0-based server IDs. Fix duplicate quality profiles in selection popup for users with multiple root folders. Add graceful error handling for Jellyfin version incompatibility in watch history collection. 2206 tests
v2.1.0.2: Improved Discovery Sidebar Navigation - tab layout can show more than 5 recommendations in one row now. Automatically reloading next recommendation after one was dismissed or requested.
v2.1.0.1: Fix Discovery sidebar navigation - tab is now found dynamically by container index regardless of user-configured tab name, instead of relying on exact text match.

v2.1.0.0: Seerr Discovery - personalized external content recommendations via Overseerr/Jellyseerr with ensemble scoring, one-click request submission, parental rating enforcement, language-based discovery, and Arr library exclusion. 2190 tests.

v2.0.0.3: Instance-based Arr config (legacy removed), persistent language/log-level. Recommendations add audio language & creation date, subtitle language affinity, collection progression boost; meaningful-interaction watched predicates. Centralized popularity scoring, richer training features (31-feature vector), series aggregation, weight schema bump. Neural MLP upgraded to 4-hidden-layer architecture (31→48→24→12→6→1, ~3097 params). Training refactored into TrainingDataBuilder + TrainingFeatureComputer. A/B testing cohort infrastructure with deterministic user bucketing and adaptive sigmoid midpoint. 2124 tests.

v2.0.0.2: Replaced decorative emojis with Material Symbols font icons for consistent cross-platform rendering. Standardized dash punctuation. Fixed subtitle orphan detection to avoid false deletions. 2110 tests.
v2.0.0.1: UI improvement - Recommendations and Watch Activity sections in the Discover tab are now collapsible. Collapsible state is preserved on user switch. 2032 tests.

v2.0.0.0: New Discover tab using an ensemble ML model to provide tailored content recommendations. This update also introduces granular activity tracking and improved system cleanup for uninstallation of this plugin. 2032 tests.

v1.2.1.0: Statistics refactored to use Jellyfin MediaStream metadata (replaces filename parsing). Dynamic range detection (HDR10, HDR10+, Dolby Vision, HLG, SDR). Extended resolution classification (8K, 1440p, SD). Differentiated audio codecs (TrueHD Atmos, DTS-X, DTS-HD MA, EAC3 Atmos). Donut chart enhancements with dynamic range visualization. Library Insights in Trends tab (top-10 largest directories, recently added/changed items, per-library size breakdown with 15-min cache). Performance improvement via per-item video stream caching. Documentation updated.

v1.2.0.0: Seerr Cleanup Task (scheduled cleanup of unavailable Overseerr/Jellyseerr media requests), Unsaved Settings Alert (dirty-tracking with discard/save/cancel dialog), Collapsible Arr/Seerr sections with dynamic instance count, Auto-Save Dropdowns (task modes + language save instantly with checkmark/cross indicator), Link Repair enhanced with symlink support, Auto-Init Scan on first visit, Scroll Position Restore after language change and backup import, 4-part versioning, meta.json fixes.
v1.1.0: Performance optimizations for GrowthTimelineService and BackupService, refactored monolith services, improved cross-platform compatibility, Trends UI enhancements.

v1.0.9: Removed legacy statistics history (replaced by growth timeline), removed Export/CSV endpoints, new StatisticsCacheService, legacy history file cleanup, growth timeline interpolation & deduplication, reduced backup size limit, 957 tests.
v1.0.8: Project restructure, bug fix for Jellyfin versions below 10.11.8, backup/restore data, enhanced TrendChart, relocated download buttons, responsive Data Tree for touch devices.
Exclude trash folders from media statistics, fix false positives for orphaned TV show metadata directories, fix trash disable dialog in UI.

Multi-instance Arr support (up to 3 Radarr + 3 Sonarr), Arr connection test endpoint, persisted latest scan results (survives restarts), post-cleanup statistics scan, embedded subtitle detection in health checks, video vs music audio codec split, codec file path tracking with clickable drill-down, trash contents detail API, trash folder management UI, trash disable dialog, other file tracking, 6-tab modular dashboard (Overview/Codecs/Health/Trends/Settings/Arr), modular CSS/JS build system, XSS protection, boxset/collection health check skipping, comprehensive README rewrite, 573 tests.

Added STRM file repair task, unified TaskMode system (Activate/DryRun/Deactivate per task), single master HelperCleanupTask replacing separate scheduled tasks, fixed ConfigVersion not preserved on settings save, fixed DI resolution for System.IO.Abstractions.IFileSystem, updated README, 315 tests.

Fixed plugin logo 404 (logo.png now included as physical file in release ZIP with meta.json imagePath), fixed SanitizeFileName null-char handling, removed duplicate Cleanup Statistics UI section, removed unused GetThumbImage method, 244 tests.

Fixed subtitle false positives (explicit ISO 639 allowlists instead of naive 2-3 letter heuristic), moved SubtitleFlags/KnownLanguageCodes to MediaExtensions, ArrIntegrationService now uses IHttpClientFactory, CleanupTrackingService thread-safety with lock, specific exception handling, removed _ = ex anti-pattern, 244 tests.
Fixed config page not loading (script/style tags moved inside page div), plugin now visible in Jellyfin sidebar menu with EnableInMainMenu, updated test count to 212.

Initial release with trickplay folder cleanup, empty media folder cleanup, orphaned subtitle cleaner, media statistics dashboard, audio codec analysis, export (JSON/CSV), historical trends, trash/recycle bin, Arr stack integration (Radarr/Sonarr), multi-language dashboard (en/de/fr/es/pt/zh/tr), library include/exclude lists, and 196 tests.

versions.changelog:
## User
- The Refresh Guide progress is now more accurate

## User
- Channels now direct play on clients that support the stream instead of always being remuxed or transcoded by the server

## Developer
- The opened source now sets SupportsDirectPlay. PlaybackInfo always disables direct stream (MediaInfoHelper), so a source that only allowed direct stream could never be picked and every tune-in fell back to DirectPlayError and a remux

## User
- A channel with no viewers now stops when its countdown reaches zero. It used to run on for two to three minutes after the last viewer left
- Tune-in cards are generated for every channel shortly after the server starts and at every guide refresh, including the refresh a save triggers, so a fresh install, an update, a new logo, or changed output settings never leave a channel opening without its card

## Developer
- The linger teardown was vetoed every time because the Jellyfin reader is served right up to the close, so the two-minute recent-delivery rule always saw a viewer at the 30s mark, and the one-shot task then gave up until the reaper backstop 90s plus a minute later. A lingering session now only counts delivery after the close (DeliveryCountsAsWatched, unit tested), and LingerTeardownAsync retries every 5s until the reaper threshold
- LiveChannelsTvService sweeps the tune-in cards 20s after construction and from every GetChannelsAsync (EnsureLogoAsync then IntroService.EnsureAsync per enabled channel, serialised, logged with its trigger); a tune-in without a card now logs it
- The Sessions tab countdown wording no longer uses an em dash or a semicolon

## User
- Tune-in is now immediate. A channel opens on a short animated card (its logo and a Starting Channel caption over flowing lines) the moment you tune in, while the content is seeked and encoded behind it, and the picture no longer waits ten seconds or more for a buffer to fill first
- The Start-up buffer setting is gone. It turned out to be a literal pause Jellyfin applied before every tune-in rather than a buffer, and the cushion it was meant to provide is now built up while you are already watching

## Developer
- Removed StartupBufferSeconds and BufferMs (Jellyfin sleeps for BufferMs in TranscodeManager.AcquireResources before launching the delivery ffmpeg, on every tune-in including adoption)
- The tune-in handover now waits for the playlist and one segment instead of the full cushion, and the endpoint reader's hold-back ramps in one segment per ten seconds of session age instead of applying from the first byte
- Segments and the encoder GOP are now three seconds, matching Jellyfin's delivery remux so every stage cuts on the same keyframes

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a live_tv icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Developer
- A channel whose filters legitimately match nothing now reuses its cached empty schedule instead of re running the full library resolve on every tune in
- Guide refreshes no longer pin every enabled channel's decoded schedule in memory forever, only channels actually being watched keep a hot copy
- Long running time of day channels now resume their schedule chain where the last window ended instead of re simulating it from the anchor at every refill, so the walk no longer grows with session length
- Code scanning cleanup across the encoder resolver, stress test, recording copy, and tune in deadline, with no behaviour changes

## Developer
- A custom stream file location is validated at save and marked on disk, and cleanup only ever deletes the plugin's own session folders, so pointing it at a folder with existing content can no longer delete that content
- Settings saved through the API are validated like the dashboard enforces them, so an out of range resolution, bitrate, session limit, or channel number is rejected with a reason instead of silently breaking streams later
- The Popular Channel's settings are validated like every other channel's
- The channel editor now edits a copy, so only Save channel persists its changes, switching channels asks before discarding unsaved edits, and a failed save shows the server's reason
- An item with a broken production year can no longer take down a chronological channel's guide build
- Generated logos and the icon font moved from the shared system temp folder into Jellyfin's cache
- Tuning in to a channel cancels a running stress test, so a real viewer always wins the encoder
- The plugin now correctly declares Jellyfin 10.11.10 as its minimum server version

## Developer
- Guide programs now carry a poster, a landscape thumb, a backdrop, and a logo instead of one image, with episodes taking their poster from the series, so every client renders the shape its layout wants
- New Start up buffer setting, defaulting to 12 seconds, sets how much of a channel is encoded before playback starts and how far ahead of you it stays. Raise it if the first seconds of a tune in stutter
- Burned in subtitles now come from the file Jellyfin extracts, so bold, italic, and colour markup survives, external subtitle files burn correctly, and attached fonts are used
- {'New subtitle appearance settings': 'font, size, text and outline colour, outline or solid box background, and bold. Untouched, subtitles render exactly as authored'}
- Streams Jellyfin reports as playing, paused included, are never closed by the stream cap, the time limit, or the idle timer. Only Kill on the Sessions tab stops a stream someone is watching
- An encoder that dies mid watch is replaced in place, continuing where it stopped, instead of ending the stream

## Developer
- Timers now produce real recordings. When a timer's window ends the aired program is resolved back to the library item it replayed and that file is placed in the Live TV recordings folder, hardlinked on the same volume or copied otherwise, with no capture or transcoding
- Recordings use the built in DVR's folder and naming scheme, honoring the server's configured recording paths and subfolder option, so they land as Series/Season folders and Movie (Year) folders the recordings library groups correctly
- The recordings folder is registered as a library when nothing serves it and a targeted refresh runs after each recording, so new recordings appear on the Recordings shelf immediately
- Record Series now works. One rule per series per channel (duplicate rules consolidate automatically and their timers follow the surviving rule), expanding into linked upcoming timers a day ahead, one per distinct episode, honoring day and time constraints. Cancelling a rule removes it and its timers
- Cancelling a timer sticks and aborts it in place, so no recording is delivered. Cancelled timers become tombstones series expansion cannot recreate, and pressing record again re arms the program
- Completed timers carry their recording path and age out of the timer list while the recording lives on as a normal library item. Failed recordings retry up to three times before the timer is marked errored
- Recording a program that already aired works, since the content it replayed already exists
- Tuning into a continuous channel deep in its loop no longer times out. The playlist now starts at the item currently airing, so the tune in seek stays inside one file instead of decoding through every prior item to reach the current position

## Developer
- DVR timers are now persisted and honored, so scheduling, listing, updating, and cancelling recordings works from any client and survives restarts
- When a channel produces no playable output the session's ffmpeg log is now surfaced in the server log, so failure reports carry the cause instead of just the symptom

## Developer
- Stop cutting items off at midnight on channels with time-of-day rating blocks
- Daypart schedules now run as one continuous chain anchored at the last configuration save, so items that cross midnight play in full

## Developer
- Serve opened streams through Jellyfin's internal live stream endpoint as a direct stream provider
- The opened stream is probed again on every server version, so playback direct streams instead of re-encoding as interlaced

## Developer
- Apply the VPP brightness gain before the tone map instead of after, matching Jellyfin's order
- Fixes washed out HDR playback when a VPP tone mapping brightness gain is set

## Developer
- Add a watchdog for tracking if there is an open channel but no sessions then closing that channel
- Prevent hanging channels and kill their ffmpeg if unused.

## Developer
- Obtain HWA device based on settings instead of falling back to 128

## Developer
- Fix a live channel dropping for the remaining viewers when one of several viewers stops watching
- Update the README for the current features

## Developer
- Add rating blocks to the Popular channel
- Tag kids per rating block
- Add News and Sports channel categories with an automatic movie tag
- Replace Extra content with Content Types toggles

## Developer
- Add time of day rating blocks with a transition window
- Add shuffle, alphabetical, and chronological loop order
- Use collections as channel sources
- Organize channel and popular settings into sub sections
- Split ChannelService into focused files

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12
- Use ActivityLogger from Base 2026.7.12
- Standardize activity log messages
- Move Stress test and Reset into a Troubleshooting section

## Developer
- Item boundaries are now timestamp-continuous - each item's timeline chains from where the previous item actually ended instead of the scheduled boundary, so seams carry no PTS jump for a client's video decoder to stall on (seen as frozen video with continuing audio on VLCKit-based players like Swiftfin)

## Developer
- Dolby Vision Profile 5 items are now excluded from schedules with a clear log line - Profile 5 has no HDR10-compatible base layer, so it renders green/purple through any tone mapper; Profile 8 and HDR10 versions play correctly and stay included
- Schedules now heal metadata runtime drift - when a full item plays through, its real length is recorded and used from the next guide refresh, closing the timestamp gap (or overlap) at item boundaries when a file's metadata runtime is wrong

## Developer
- HDR letterbox bars are now true black on the Intel GPU pipeline - padding happens after the tone map, so the bars are painted in SDR space instead of being run through the HDR-to-SDR LUT (which rendered them green)
- HDR brightness now honours Jellyfin's VPP Tone mapping brightness/contrast gain (Dashboard > Playback > Transcoding), applied after the GPU tone map, so channels match regular playback instead of rendering dark
- Internal cleanup - removed the unused Windows QSV legacy paths (vendor-matched HDR chain, interlaced/10-bit decode workarounds), refreshed comments to describe current behaviour, and rewrote the README to be concise and current

## Developer
- First tune-in no longer stalls on large channels - freshly built schedules stay in memory after each guide refresh instead of being reloaded (or silently rebuilt) on the tune-in critical path, and any slow or failed schedule load is now visible in the log
- Subtitle burn-in now stays on the GPU for Intel hardware - the subtitle renders on the CPU and is composited in VRAM (overlay_vaapi), so Forced-only channels playing foreign-language 4K/HDR keep full GPU speed instead of dropping to the software chain
- Compatible with Jellyfin 10.11.10 - the opened-source probe (the interlace workaround) is now version-gated, fixing total playback failure on 10.11.10 servers
- Sessions tab - selecting a session opens its ffmpeg log in a modal with Refresh, Copy, and Kill; logs are cached per session and removed when the session closes; the speed column now shows the ratio next to the status dot

## Developer
- The Sessions tab shows when a viewerless stream is winding down (with its countdown), and its Kill button now stops the encoder immediately instead of waiting out the wind-down
- New encoder stress test on the Settings tab - pick a demanding library item and the server measures how many concurrent streams it can sustain with the real channel pipeline, recommending the Maximum concurrent streams value
- Fully GPU-resident Intel pipeline (Linux QSV/VAAPI) - decode, deinterlace, scale, tone map, and encode all stay in VRAM on Jellyfin's configured render node. Benchmarked on an N100 iGPU with 4K HDR10 HEVC, 2.6x faster than the old download-to-CPU chain; the Intel 10-bit and interlaced software-decode workarounds are gone, and HDR tone maps scale-first (1.9x faster, same picture)

## Developer
- Channels now play with a lossless remux instead of a full re-encode, fixing the false Interlaced video is not supported transcode Jellyfin forces on every live-TV stream (the opened stream is probed so the real, progressive format wins)
- Much faster channel start-up, with the client buffer filling at full speed instead of realtime
- Streams no longer fall behind over long watches - every encoder start bursts exactly the wall-clock time the session has lost, so item transitions self-heal
- Fixed a playlist write race that could crash Jellyfin's stream reader (ffmpeg exit 139) and kill playback mid-session
- Channels degrade gracefully - standby appears within seconds when a library is unreachable, and a repeatedly failing encoder backs off instead of relaunching forever
- Removed the pre-render/warm-splice pipeline and the playback buffer, pre-render, stream window, and producer rate settings - pacing, buffering, and the disk window are now automatic and self-tuning
- Item transitions cut segments exactly on the 4-second boundary (2-second GOP alignment)
- Re-tuning a channel within 30 seconds is now instant - the still-warm encoder is adopted by the new stream instead of cold-starting a fresh one
- Faster tune-in - the stream probe analysis window was halved, and the channel logo no longer resolves before the encoder starts

Live-TV Control Center.description: Show personal or shared channel groups in the original Jellyfin Android TV / Fire TV guide, with a web EPG, remote playback, channel access rules and native app folders.
Live-TV Control Center.overview: Your channel groups in the original TV guide, plus web EPG and remote playback

versions.changelog:
- Administrators can now copy central groups into their own personal collection when switching back to personal mode, or import them later. Both management screens require an explicit copy/skip choice on mode switch. Existing personal groups take precedence when IDs match; central groups and other users' personal groups remain untouched. Custom group images are copied with newly imported groups.
- Require administrators to explicitly choose whether to copy their personal groups when switching to central management. The no-copy choice preserves personal groups for later use, and both the web dialog and plugin dashboard offer a later import. Reject an ambiguous mode-switch request instead of silently showing an empty central group list.

- Support Wholphin in the native Live TV guide: select a group or **All channels** directly in its compatible Control Center folders, then open **Live TV → TV Guide**. Group selection applies only to the authenticated user's device, respects current group/channel permissions, and restores the full guide on reset. Wholphin does not support an automatic guide jump.
- Add administrator switches for the official Jellyfin Android TV / Fire TV app and Wholphin. A sole eligible TV is selected automatically; with several TVs, the last available choice is remembered per user. Disabled or disconnected devices cannot receive playback or guide changes.
- Add recognizable artwork to the Control Center home tile, guide actions, confirmation and fallback folders. **All channels** has its own EPG-reset image; created groups have a distinct group image. Personal and shared groups can use custom PNG, JPEG or WebP images up to 5 MiB, with preview and reset controls and permission checks.
- Add recording controls to the grouped web EPG. Users with Jellyfin's Live TV management permission can schedule, edit and cancel single-program or series timers, including padding and series options; recording errors remain visible in the dialog.
- Restore reliable loading of the independent web EPG behind reverse proxies that cached its old script URL. Preserve original channel logos, official Android TV / Fire TV behavior, channel playback and the existing plugin identity and settings.

- Selecting a group in the official Android TV / Fire TV app immediately applies that group's native guide scope and opens the ordinary Live TV view. The separate Native TV guide action remains available to retry.
- Hide direct grouped-channel media tiles from that authenticated TV response while keeping the native guide action and browsable program-list fallback. Internal channel items and playlists remain unchanged.
- Retain per-user/device validation, group access checks and safe behavior when navigation is unavailable. The original app may still require selecting TV Guide after opening Live TV; a direct timeline deep link is not exposed by the stock client.

- Organize Live TV channels in ordered personal groups independent of IPTV-provider categories, or use administrator-managed shared groups with per-group user access.
- Show one selected group's original channels in Jellyfin's native Android TV / Fire TV timeline. Select the group on the TV or from the web/mobile page; the web page can also apply the deduplicated union of all visible groups. Reset to all ordinarily permitted channels at any time. Selections are per user and TV device.
- Browse an independent web EPG with a channel/program timeline, now/next/later programs, channel cards, day/time navigation and zoom. Save visible/default groups and view preferences; use the interface in English or German.
- Use the web or phone guide as a remote for the official Jellyfin Android TV / Fire TV app: discover a compatible TV, remember the target, and start or switch live channels while the guide stays open.
- Apply optional central channel-access rules to selected users, including children's accounts. Restrictions cover the plugin and ordinary Jellyfin Live TV, direct playback, playlists and associated recordings while preserving Jellyfin permissions.
- Browse grouped channel and daily program folders in supported native apps; optionally mirror groups as playlists for other clients.
- Integrate the web interface through File Transformation, optionally add a Plugin Pages menu shortcut, customize the display name and hide the original Live TV home tile when the groups entry is available.
- Support Jellyfin 12.0 or later in the Jellyfin 12 series (12.1 confirmed). Keep the existing plugin ID, channel identity and stored settings for upgrades from Live-TV Groups. Native guide navigation may require one additional TV Guide selection; no virtual channels or custom TV client are used.

Local Intros.description: Select a flashy pre-roll from local storage to run before any video content. Marquee Companion.description: Adds four independent capabilities: server-side filtering by media-stream characteristics that Jellyfin's core API can't express (video dynamic range, codecs, audio channel count, and spatial audio), plus opt-in global recent-podcast discovery via Podcast Index using administrator-provided credentials, plus opt-in passwordless sign-in by emailed magic link over administrator-configured SMTP, plus an opt-in scheduled task that recovers the release date of items that arrived without one by reading it from the file name. The filtering API exposes a paginated, BaseItemDto-compatible endpoint and a capability endpoint for client feature-detection.
Marquee Companion.overview: Media-stream filtering, opt-in podcast discovery, email sign-in, and release-date recovery.

versions.changelog:
- Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.
- Release-date recovery is chosen PER LIBRARY. - Added opt-in release-date recovery. Downloaded YouTube content carries its upload
  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.
- Adds the seamless Marquee Companion panel to Jellyfin Web without manual web-client changes. - Adds paired Jellyfin 10/.NET 9 and Jellyfin 12/.NET 10 package builds.

  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.
- Release-date recovery is chosen PER LIBRARY. - Added opt-in release-date recovery. Downloaded YouTube content carries its upload
  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.

  formats may be missing. It is fetched only when absent, and there is nothing to configure.

  degraded. The resolve timeout moves from 10 to 30 seconds to accommodate runtime start-up
  and signature deciphering; a timeout would otherwise surface as a silently missing trailer.

  channel. It is visible and controllable under Dashboard → Scheduled Tasks, does nothing
  unless a tracking source has automatic updates enabled, and never advances a pinned
  version. The newest three builds per channel are retained so a bad build can be rolled
  back by pinning the previous one, without a download.

# 🎬 Media Bar Arrives on Jellyfin 12

Media Bar **3.0.0.0** brings support for **Jellyfin 12**, including compatibility with both the classic desktop experience and Jellyfin's newer modern web layout.

> ## 🙌 Huge thanks to MakD and the upstream contributors
>
> Media Bar itself is the work of **MakD and the contributors to the upstream Media Bar project**. The plugin I maintain is primarily a Jellyfin wrapper around that work, exposing configuration and integration points so it can be installed and managed cleanly as a Jellyfin plugin.
>
> A huge amount of effort has gone into keeping Media Bar working across Jellyfin's changing web interface, especially for Jellyfin 12. The features, UI work and frontend improvements in this release are built on that upstream work, and the credit for that belongs to **MakD and everyone contributing there**.
>
> My part is largely packaging, integrating and exposing that work through Jellyfin's plugin system.

## ✨ New Features

* Added support for **Jellyfin 12**.
* Added support for Jellyfin 12's **modern React/MUI home screen layout**, alongside the existing classic desktop layout.
* Updated the bundled Media Bar frontend to the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream version.
* Added Jellyfin 12-specific styling so Media Bar integrates correctly with the new web-client shell while retaining the existing appearance on the classic layout.
* Media Bar continues to ship its frontend assets directly with the plugin, ensuring the version displayed in Jellyfin matches the plugin version you've installed.

## 🛠️ Improvements

* Synced Media Bar with the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream work.
* Improved Media Bar placement within the Jellyfin 12 home screen across both supported layouts.
* Improved layout behaviour on taller displays, ensuring Jellyfin's home-screen rows remain below the Media Bar content rather than overlapping its controls.
* Improved localisation handling when loading Jellyfin's translation chunks.
* Retained support for the **Get updates early** option for users who explicitly want to track unreleased upstream Media Bar changes.

## 🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed Media Bar being inserted in the wrong position when using Jellyfin 12's modern layout (#181).
* Fixed translated Media Bar strings falling back to English or producing JSON decoding errors for some languages (#185).
* Fixed home-screen rows overlapping Media Bar buttons on taller viewports.
* Fixed Jellyfin 12 layout differences that could cause Media Bar to render incorrectly compared with Jellyfin 10.11.

## ⚠️ Compatibility

* **Media Bar 3.0.0.0 supports Jellyfin 10.11.11 and Jellyfin 12.**
* Users on older Jellyfin 10.x versions should remain on a compatible **2.x** Media Bar release.
* Jellyfin 12 support includes both the **classic Desktop layout** and the newer **modern React/MUI layout**.
* A compatible **File Transformation 3.x** release is required.
* If you're using the **Get updates early** option, unreleased upstream Media Bar changes may behave differently from the frontend bundled and tested with this plugin release.

## Contributors

* austinnorgaard
* judarange

## ❤️ Support

If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27).

Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

1.0.7.4 is a small follow-up to 1.0.7.3's combined audio + subtitle cleanup pass, closing the last case where MediaDash could ffmpeg the same file twice in one fix run.

When a file had a queued re-encode AND queued track cleanup (unwanted audio or subtitle languages), it used to remux for the tracks first and then re-encode a second time. The re-encode already drops unwanted tracks by itself, so the first remux was wasted work — and if it didn't run first, it would fail with "nothing to remove" once the re-encode had finished. Now the fix run detects the overlap and lets the re-encode handle both jobs in one pass. Same recycle bin entry, one history row per issue, both track and quality issues flip to Fixed together.

User-visible impact: multi-language 4K remuxes that also need size reduction finish in half the time, and the Errors tab stops picking up spurious "nothing to remove" failures on files that were just re-encoded.

Duplicate detection: keys now include ProductionYear so remakes stop collapsing (#3), keeper picker excludes symlinks and 0-byte files (F-098), DuplicateMinAgeDays default 7 to 0 with one INFO line naming vetoed count.

Playability: cross-checks ffprobe format_name against extension so an MKV renamed .mp3 emits container-extension-mismatch (F-213). HasTruncationMarker no longer treats the benign Truncating packet warning as truncation - that warning fires on real-world MKV cluster boundaries, MPEG-TS packet alignment, and MP4 mdat overlap on files that play fine in Jellyfin (Reddit reports: friskyapple, oogoom, moonplaza, Commercial-Camp-8052). Only File ended prematurely now counts.

TrackFixer ffmpeg command gains -fflags +genpts at input and -avoid_negative_ts make_zero at output - fixes the mpegts sample rate not set / Could not write header failure on Blu-ray-derived .m2ts sources, and lets OutputVerifier accept legitimate long-form duration drift (#39, slack widened from fixed 2 s to max(2 s, dur x 2 percent)).

Combined ffmpeg pass (#28, #32): FixTask now detects same-file AudioLanguage + SubtitleLanguage pairs before the fix loop and routes them through a new TrackFixer.FixCombinedAsync so one ffmpeg drops both categories in a single pass instead of two back-to-back remuxes. - DuplicateTitleJaccardVeto (default 0.40): kills pairs whose filename title tokens overlap less than this.
- DuplicateRuntimeVetoPct (default 15%): kills pairs whose runtimes differ by more than this.

Duplicate detection rework with a per-pair confidence ladder (Exact 1.00 / Identified 0.90 / Heuristic 0.70) plus two hard vetoes (title-token Jaccard, runtime delta) that kill the GitHub #3 Futurama-specials false-positive class.

Fixes
- GitHub #3 - duplicate false positives on distinct files sharing an episode metadata slot.
- GitHub #12 - container CPU/RAM cards showed HOST numbers; now read cgroup v2 -> v1 first and fall through to /proc only when unbounded.
- GitHub #6 + #12-SMART - Linux SMART reported Unknown forever on drives whose libraries live on a partition; now walks partition -> disk via lsblk.
- ArtworkFixer clears the item's ImageInfos BEFORE deleting the file on disk so /Items/{id}/Images/Primary stops 404-ing after a corrupt-artwork sweep.
- Dry-run is now airtight: MissingSubtitleFixer no longer queries external subtitle providers under dry-run (was leaking which files exist and burning provider quota).
- Field report A1: default-threaded ffmpeg pinned every core on a 1-2 vCPU Docker VM and locked up SSH. Threads default to max(1, ProcessorCount/2).
- Field reports A9/A10: reworded 'original kept in recycle bin' and dry-run preview action text so users stop reading it as 'MediaDash is hoarding files'.
- Field report B1: sidecars now follow the primary file after a successful move.
- Field report B4: subtitles in Subtitles/ or Subs/ subfolders next to media are detected.
- Field report D2: MissingSubtitle now runs before Transcode so subtitles land before an encode that would rename-orphan them.
- NfoScanner no longer flags valid metadata as corrupt on missing per-Actor extensions or trailing text after </movie>.
- OrphanCleanupScanner: unrelated adjacent folders no longer treated as orphans; scanners emitting non-video paths opt out of scoped-delete so stale rows don't sit forever.
- EmbeddedCoverArtScanner: no longer flags every non-trivial AVI as corrupt.
- SmartHealth probe: no longer stuck on 'Checking SMART status...' forever on probe crash; PowerShell reliability-counter fallback no longer silently misses on trailing whitespace in FriendlyName.
- RecycleBin cross-volume move: .mediadash.tmp staging file is cleaned up when a move throws mid-way.
- LibraryMonitor: ReportFileSystemChanged now fires for both source and destination on move so cached ImageInfo drops.

Privacy
- Anonymous community-stats install ID is now month-rotated: SHA-256(salt || Jellyfin SystemId || year-month), never stored on disk. Prior persistent UUID was stronger linkability than APP/GDPR tolerates for 'aggregate community stats'.

Full-scanner community stats, on-by-default opt-in, and first-run wizard layout polish. Dashboard's fix-completion popup and redownload banner now survive a plugin reload.

Features
- Community stats now cover every scanner MediaDash ships. 8 new scanners added to the payload, backend schema, and public views (Ungrouped, LargeTrickplay, SubtitleFonts, OrphanedDebris, CorruptNfo, HeavyTranscode, FailedTranscode, EmbeddedCoverArt) alongside the existing 10.
- Community stats default flipped from off to on for new installs. Existing installs are unchanged; their persisted AnalyticsEnabled value wins. The first-run wizard shows the checkbox pre-ticked; untick in Settings -> Safety at any time to opt out.
- Dashboard's LastFixRun (fix-completion popup) and RedownloadWarnings (Overview banner) are now persisted to the plugin DB via a write-through wrapper. Previously both dropped on every plugin reload, so a mid-day restart made the popup or banner vanish. Rehydrated on plugin start.
- README's community-impact table, docs/index.html impact section, and the monthly-stats GitHub Actions workflow now render rows for all 18 scanner types. docs/PRIVACY.md field table extended to match; opt-out language rewritten throughout.
- Docs screenshots (overview, issues, history, settings) regenerated against the current UI with Blender open-movie sample data - no personal filenames or hostnames.

Bug fixes
- First-run wizard "Skip walkthrough" now mints the anonymous install UUID when analytics is enabled. Previously, skipping the wizard left the ID empty and the reporter silently no-op'd, so an on-by-default install that never completed the walkthrough never actually contributed a single row.
- Wizard step 5 (Oversized files): "Skip HDR files" now sits to the right of "Preferred GPU" in a two-column flex row instead of stacked below the description. Both controls align to the same height.
- Wizard step 8 (Language cleanup): the mdChipInput language pickers no longer sit taller than the emby-select controls next to them. Same 46px height rule that already applied on the Settings tab now applies inside the wizard too.
- Wizard step 2 (Libraries): the "Check library access" button now uses the plugin's mdActionBtn class (rounded pill, primary accent, 44px tall) instead of Jellyfin's raw raised-button styling. Matches the rest of the plugin.
- Wizard step 16 (Community stats): intro copy no longer starts with "Off by default -" and now lists every scanner in the "What's sent" panel.

Reclaim totals now match across the plugin, heavy-transcode fixer works on well-encoded sources, SMART shows correctly on unprivileged Linux, and the History tab lets you slice failures by reason.

Features
- History tab's Failed filter now surfaces a "search by reason" dropdown listing the distinct failure reasons in your history with a count each (Permission denied, I/O error, Cross-device link, File no longer exists, etc.). Selecting one narrows the list; switching the top-level chip clears it.
- SMART pill on the Overview drives now shows a specific hint when smartctl fails due to permissions on Linux: setcap 'cap_sys_rawio+ep' $(which smartctl) for native installs, --cap-add=SYS_RAWIO --device=... for Docker.

Bug fixes
- Overview "Reclaimed since install" and History tab's summary + per-library chart now show the same number. History was summing the paginated 500-row window client-side while Overview summed the entire history server-side, causing the mismatch (e.g. 599 GB vs 8.1 GB). New /History/Stats endpoint aggregates over all history server-side; both panels source the total from it.
- Heavy-transcode / failed-transcode fixes no longer refuse to swap when the re-encoded file is slightly larger than the original. Those fix types exist for direct-play compatibility, not disk savings â€” the size gate is now Quality-only, with a 30% hard cap on the transcode types to guard against misconfigured encode settings.
- SMART pills now appear on library drives on Linux. Library-drive detection was using Path.GetPathRoot which always returns "/" on Linux â€” no library drive was ever flagged, so the SMART probe never ran there. Now uses the deepest-matching mount point via FindDriveForPath.
- smartctl exit_status is now honoured. Non-zero exit (permission denied, unsupported device, no SMART support) returns Unknown with the actual smartctl error message, instead of being mis-interpreted as "self-assessment FAILED".

Features

Post-1.0 UI polish and a recycle-bin config regression fix.

Bug fixes
- RecycleBin path no longer requires library-adjacency. Users can point the bin at any writable location (e.g. `/mnt/media/.mediadash-recycle` as a sibling of the library for cross-volume-free moves). Only OS-reserved roots (/etc, /bin, /usr, Windows System32, etc.) are refused.
- Errors tab: badge no longer shows a stale count (e.g. "691") after the tab has been cleared. The periodic status poll now delegates to loadErrors() when the user is on the Errors tab, so badge + list update from the same fetch.
- Issues tab: badge is now sourced from the actual issue list length, so "999+" no longer disagrees with the visible cards.
- Overview issue-shortcut cards now show reclaimable space (bytes / MB / GB) as the primary number, with the file count as a subtitle. Types with no space-savings info still show the raw count.
- Progress bar activity text now spans the full width of the scan-state line above it (was capped at 36em).
- Removed the second empty "Subtitles" settings card that appeared post-1.0 (SubtitleFonts controls are already folded into the SubtitleLanguage card).
- "Collapse all" / "Expand all" button on Settings now truthfully reflects what a click will do: it excludes force-collapsed Off-mode tasks from the state check, and hides itself entirely when nothing on the page is togglable.

- Ungrouped-media grouper and Corrupt-artwork scanner now fully wired into the UI (types, settings card, per-type mode).
- ISO 639-1 (2-letter) language tags fold to ISO 639-2 via CultureInfo so "en" matches ["eng"] and single-language audio tracks stop getting flagged for removal.
- Opportunistic 15-minute fix scheduling with idle deferral; automatic migration from legacy DailyTrigger on first boot.
- Post-Jellyfin-12 upgrade cleanup that sweeps orphaned trickplay folders on first launch.
- Book (EPUB / PDF / MOBI / AZW3) and comic (CBZ / CBR / CB7) integrity probes.
- Corrupt-artwork, orphan-cleanup, trickplay-optimize, embedded-cover-art, heavy-transcode, failed-transcode and NFO-integrity scanners.
- File browser tab (rename / move / delete / upload inside library boundaries, deletes go to the recycle bin).
- Per-GPU picker + hardware-accelerated re-encoding (AMF / NVENC / QSV / VideoToolbox) with automatic software fallback.
- Errors tab with copy-diagnostics-for-bug-report button.

Bug fixes
- RecycleBin cross-volume moves verify copy size before deleting the source (no more silent data loss on truncated writes).
- MoveToBin folder names carry a per-batch GUID so same-millisecond recycles no longer collide.
- FileBrowser rename / move now return 409 on concurrent-target creation instead of silently overwriting.
- Upload endpoint rejects oversized bodies via Content-Length pre-flight before any disk I/O; 50 GB per-file cap.
- LibraryGuard refuses paths whose ancestor chain contains a symlink or NTFS junction.
- RecycleBinPath must sit inside the plugin data dir or a configured library; OS-reserved roots refused.
- SweepOrphanSidecars enumerates with reparse-point skip and re-checks each candidate before delete.
- IsSimpleName refuses Windows reserved names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9) and trailing dot / space.
- RelocateIssuePaths uses COLLATE NOCASE on the boundary match so sibling issues re-point correctly after case-varying moves on Windows.
- PlayabilityFixer re-verify is reason-driven (audio-kind files no longer recycled on "no-audio" false positives; size-truncated files now actually removed).
- TrackFixer.IsSelfReferentialSubtitle normalises both paths via Path.GetFullPath so legacy relative-path issue rows can't trick the guard.
- MediaSorterFixer cross-volume detection works on Linux (was previously blind because Path.GetPathRoot returns "/").
- MissingSubtitleFixer catches TaskCanceledException from provider network stalls without aborting the whole fix run.
- smartctl / nvidia-smi / df invocations use ArgumentList (no shell tokenization); absolute-path resolution on Linux where possible.
- WMI drive-letter validated before WQL interpolation.
- BulkUpdateOpenIssueStatus chunks at 500 params; controller caps requests at 50 k IDs.
- SmartHealthProbe stdout and stderr drained concurrently before WaitForExit (no more pipe-buffer deadlocks on large SMART payloads).
- Diagnostics ring buffer dedup keys off a hash of the pre-truncation message; entries are replaced (not mutated) so concurrent Recent() callers can't observe torn reads.
- AssSubtitleFile.Parse caps input at 100 MB to prevent OOM on malformed sidecars.
- Wizard i18n guard relaxed to Math.min so partial locale translations override index-by-index instead of falling back entirely to English.
- Retention slider in Settings now runs to 365 days (matched the wizard, no more silent 90-day cap on save).
- Update banner no longer fires on 0.0.0.0 dev builds.
- AnalyticsEnabled default flipped to false to match every "off by default" string in the UI.
- Task-active count derived from FIX_TYPES.length (previously hardcoded "of 15", now correct for all 18 fix types).
- Obsolete ScheduledFixTime config field removed.

Bug-fix bundle over 0.9.9.3.

Duplicate detector no longer flags different files with a shared prefix as duplicates. Replaced the trailing-tag whitelist (which kept missing new suffix combos users reported) with file-name-based edition detection: any variation in the filename between two TMDb-matched files yields a different edition key when 'Treat editions as duplicates' is off. Covers 100% of possible suffix combinations. Byte-identical copies with the same filename still group as duplicates. Regression: 'StarWarsCloneWars2003 - Connecting the Dots.mkv' vs 'StarWarsCloneWars2003 - Bridging the Saga.mkv' â€” now stays as two separate entries.

Jellyfin sidecar files/folders are skipped by the Duplicate scanner before grouping â€” no more 'theme.mp3 in show1/ is a duplicate of theme.mp3 in show2/' reports. Covers theme/themevideo/poster/backdrop/logo/etc plus extras subfolders (extras, trailers, behind the scenes, deleted scenes, featurettes, ...) and per-item extras suffixes in both compact and spaced form ('-behindthescenes' and '- Behind the scenes'). Reference: https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/server/media/movies/#extras

Dismiss button on issue cards renamed to 'Ignore this' â€” the existing behaviour already blocks that file from re-reporting, the old label was just confusing.

New: notification badges on Issues (open count, cyan), History (failed rows count, amber), and Errors tabs (unchanged).

Version scheme: feature.feature.feature.bugfix â€” fourth digit increments for hotfixes.

New Overview banner warns when a MediaDash re-encode gets undone by something external (typically Sonarr/Radarr redownloading a "too-small" file whose size dropped below the quality profile minimum, but also fires on manual recycle-bin restores or backup-restore overwrites).

Detection is evidence-based, not guessed: at the end of every scan MediaDash walks the last 30 days of successful non-dry-run history entries, and for each one where the ORIGINAL is still preserved in the recycle bin, compares the file currently at the same path against the recycled original. If the current file is within 10% of the original size â€” i.e. the same rough size we shrank down â€” the shrunk copy has been replaced. Only paths meeting that concrete size-match trigger the warning. False positives are limited to genuine restores, which are also worth surfacing.

The red banner shows the filename, the shrunk-to size, the current size, and the fix date. Dismissable per browser session; reappears on the next scan if the condition still holds.

Two fixes and a reclaim.

VAAPI hardware encodes now pass -rc_mode VBR to hevc_vaapi / h264_vaapi / av1_vaapi. Mesa VAAPI's default rate-control is CQP, which ignores -b:v/-maxrate and picks a QP that routinely produces output LARGER than a modest-bitrate source â€” the "the re-encoded file would be larger than the original, so the original was kept" retry loop that some AMD iGPU users saw every 30-70 minutes on the same file. VBR honours -b:v as the target and -maxrate as the ceiling, so the encoder actually stays under the requested bitrate.

Orphan sidecar sweep: at the end of every fix run (right after the recycle bin purge), MediaDash now walks each library root and deletes any *.mediadash.tmp*, *.mediadash.new*, mediadash.tmp.*, or mediadash.new.* file it finds. These are leftovers from a hard-killed encode (SIGKILL, container restart, Jellyfin crash) where the C# finally block that normally deletes them never ran. Deleted-count + reclaimed-bytes go into Jellyfin's log.

FfmpegExecutor now sweeps for orphaned MediaDash ffmpeg processes before spawning a new encode. Linux only (reads /proc/<pid>/cmdline; Windows/macOS would need extra deps for a very rare failure mode). Any ffmpeg whose command line contains a mediadash.tmp or mediadash.new marker is killed with SIGKILL and its sidecar output file is deleted. Prevents the "two ffmpegs writing to the same output" scenario after a plugin hot-reload or a Jellyfin restart mid-encode. Also cleans up the interleaved-bytes .tmp file that would otherwise sit on disk until the next fix run on the same source overwrote it.

Manual fix runs now pause instead of bailing when someone starts watching. Click "Run fixes now", the queue drains as before, but if the pause-on-playback check trips between files the run pauses (with an amber banner: "Paused: someone is watching. Click 'Ignore activity' to resume anyway.") and re-checks every 30 seconds. When the viewer stops or you hit the Ignore activity button, the run resumes from where it stopped. Scheduled runs keep the previous behaviour (break on activity, next 15-minute tick tries again). The Ignore flag only applies to the current run â€” a fresh Run fixes now click brings the pause behaviour back.

Fix the "Fix run finished with failures" popup firing on every page load. The first-poll guard checked prevFinishedAt !== undefined but lastStatus starts as null, which short-circuited prevFinishedAt to null (not undefined) â€” so opening the plugin page always fired an alert if the most-recent completed run had any failures, even while a new run was still going. The alert now only fires when a poll's FinishedAtUtc actually changes from a prior poll.

Fix cascade after 0.9.3 hit real prod hardware. Track-remux fixer now uses the same hash-fallback sidecar name as the transcode fixer (v0.9.2 shipped it for one path, not both) â€” long-UTF-8 filenames (Cyrillic/CJK) no longer fail with ffmpeg "Error opening output" on Linux NAME_MAX. Free-disk-space check now looks at the actual mount containing the file via RecycleBin.FindDriveForPath, not the root filesystem â€” LXC/Docker setups where /mnt/media is a large bind-mount but / is a tiny rootfs no longer get false "Not enough free disk space" bailouts on 30-60 GB BDRemuxes. QualityScanner is less trigger-happy: dropped the container-level bitrate fallback (was flagging remuxes with big lossless audio as "video too fat"), and added a 15%-of-file-size minimum-savings gate so HEVC->HEVC recompression at close bitrates doesn't burn a 20-minute encode only for the fixer to abort with "the re-encoded file would be larger than the original". TrackFixer's error truncation matches TranscodeFixer now â€” keeps the ffmpeg-error tail (where the real reason lives), not the head.

Transcode fix now actually uses the GPU. v0.9.2 shipped without the hardware-encoder path wired in â€” the UseHardwareEncoder toggle had no effect and every re-encode ran on the CPU via libx265. This release wires the hw path through and adds full VAAPI support (device auto-picked from /dev/dri/renderD* or Jellyfin's VaapiDevice, with format=nv12,hwupload / scale_vaapi in the filter chain). When Jellyfin's own HardwareAccelerationType is unset, the plugin now autodetects: NVIDIA â†’ NVENC, any Linux DRM device (Intel/AMD iGPU or dGPU) â†’ VAAPI, Windows â†’ AMF (or QSV for Intel iGPUs), macOS â†’ VideoToolbox, and falls back to libx265 only when no GPU is present. Any hardware failure still retries with software so no encode gets stuck. Settings page tidy-up: 'Thorough playability check' no longer has the oversized inset box beside the disposal dropdown; Issues tab drops the redundant 'Show' type filter (the count pills already do that) and moves the filename search onto the same row.

Mind the Gaps.description: Scans your library for gaps (missing movies in partially-owned collections and franchises, missing series content, unowned titles from actor and director filmographies, and related recommendations) using TMDB, Trakt, TheTVDB, and TVmaze, with music and book sources (MusicBrainz, OpenLibrary, Discogs), and reads the watchlists and want-lists you already keep on those sites. Presents an easy todo list for filling out your collection, diagnoses why a title is reported missing, surfaces where to watch each item, and can optionally mint native virtual placeholders for missing items.
Mind the Gaps.overview: Find what's missing and related in your library and build a todo list to complete it.

versions.changelog: 10.11.10.0 - The Maintenance section has a Fulfillment queue for an administrator who fetches titles by hand. It folds every user's TODO list into one row per title, sorted by how many people still want it, names who is still waiting, and shows the streaming-service icons as soon as the queue opens, with the same links a TODO row already has. Mark fetched closes the title for every requester in one action, and Verify all checks the queue against the library and closes a title you already have, however it arrived. With Everyone's watchlist on (off by default), that same household list is a Discover source and leads the Discover view of every domain it has entries for. Send to the acquisition stack is done from the Gaps Report. The report's Send action has a quality profile picker, filled from the stack's own profile list and preselecting the profile you configured, so an older title the default profile cannot find a release for can still be sent. The report's My TODO list popup is gone; the Fulfillment queue is where an administrator sees every list. The report's multi-select bar can Acquire, Request, or Resolve a checked batch (Resolve applies one shared note), alongside Mint and Add to TODO. An administrator can manage another user's want-to-watch list. With "Want to watch: move arrived titles into a playlist" on, a title that is in the library moves into that user's own Jellyfin playlist the next time it is verified, so it shows up in every client. The playlist is named Want to Watch unless you change it, and only a real file counts as arrived. Amazon and web-search links for a book or album include the author or artist, on the report, the Web UI, and the Fulfillment queue. TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and OpenLibrary subjects are set with the same chip pickers the other curated sources use. A book's dialog loads its description from OpenLibrary when you open it. Studio pages, off by default, add a Missing from the studio row of that studio's movies you do not own, on the list page you open from a movie's studio credit. A library that sets a metadata fetcher order keeps TVmaze in the series check. TVmaze is not a Jellyfin metadata fetcher, so it is always asked and ranked last.

TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and OpenLibrary subjects are set with the same chip pickers the other curated sources use. A book's dialog loads its description from OpenLibrary when you open it. Studio pages, off by default, add a Missing from the studio row of that studio's movies you do not own, on the list page you open from a movie's studio credit. A library that sets a metadata fetcher order keeps TVmaze in the series check. TVmaze is not a Jellyfin metadata fetcher, so it is always asked and ranked last.

10.11.9.0 - Mind the Gaps now reaches into Jellyfin's own pages through an experimental, opt-in Web UI, with a master switch and one toggle per surface in settings, all off by default. A person's page lists what they made that you do not own, a movie or series page suggests titles like it that you are missing, an artist's page lists the albums you do not have, and a book page or an author's own page lists more by the same author. The home page can show a Discover row of the recommendations your scans found from titles you own and from lists that are public by nature (TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and TMDB's own feeds), never from a watchlist, wantlist, favorites, or a personal list. Click a card for a detail dialog with TMDB's synopsis, genres, runtime, rating, a trailer link, and a link to the title's JustWatch page, then send it to Radarr or Sonarr with the quality profile you pick; the dialog and the card grids can be driven from a keyboard or a TV remote. A user with a parental rating limit is shown none of these sections. With Want to watch turned on, every card carries a bookmark that adds the title to your own list, and the home page can show a Want to watch row of what you have listed and do not yet own. The TODO list is now kept per user, in the plugin's data folder, and removed when the user is deleted; the first administrator to open the old shared list takes it over, and an administrator can switch the report's TODO to everyone's lists to see and manage them. The Gaps Report loads faster: it fetches one tab at a time as slim rows, fetches a row's details only when you open it, revalidates what it already holds instead of downloading it again, and loads its script and stylesheet as separately cached files; the saved report is stored as one file per domain, and an existing report is converted automatically. A row shows up to two streaming-service icons, following your provider and monetization filters and wearing the service's logo (a service TMDB lists as several providers, such as a "with Ads" tier, shows as one icon and one provider filter entry), and clicking them opens the title's TMDB watch page. Gaps left behind by a source you have since removed or turned off are pruned on every scan, and a Prune stale gaps button under Maintenance does it right away. A TMDB list that cannot be read, such as a private one, no longer stops the other lists from being scanned, filling in a large library's series content is done in batches, and the scan log says how long each source took. New, and off by default: the report and the Web UI can load their posters, covers, and streaming-service logos through your server instead of each browser fetching them from TMDB and the other providers. Turn on "Keep the pages' images on this server" in the new Images section of settings; the server fetches each image once, from a fixed list of provider hosts only, keeps it under its cache folder, and sends the browser on to the provider whenever it cannot serve one, and a "Trim the image cache" scheduled task keeps the cache to the size you set (500 MB by default).

10.11.8.0 - The Gaps Report is reorganized around your library's domains: Movies, Shows, Music, and Books are now the primary tabs, each badged with its own gap count, with Set completion, Creator works, and Discover scoped underneath as a view you pick per domain, so only the active domain's data is loaded at a time. A Compact view toggle switches to a denser layout. Click a title to expand its detail in place: the overview, where to watch, and (outside Compact view) every information and action button tile inline instead of opening separate popovers; collapsed, the same actions live behind three icon popovers on the row, and a collapsed title's own browser tooltip shows its overview with no click at all. The toolbar is split into a filter row and an action row, and the settings page is reorganized into one collapsible section per provider (TMDB, Trakt, MDBList, Discogs, OpenLibrary, TheTVDB, IMDb, JustWatch), each badged on or off, with a search box that opens whichever section matches. Four new TMDB feeds, Top Rated, Popular, Upcoming, and Now Playing, can be turned on individually under Discover, and Jellyfin 12.0 is now a supported target alongside 10.11, each release building and shipping its own ABI-matched package. Gaps now show real cover art for books (bibliography and subject lists), music (MusicBrainz discography and artist works), and series completion episodes (TMDB, TheTVDB, and TVmaze all supply a still where they have one) instead of a blank thumbnail, falling back to the placeholder rather than a broken-image icon when a cover fails to load; MDBList entries carry a poster and description like every other source. A creator's page can be trimmed further with a minimum TMDB vote count for a movie credit and a minimum episode count for a TV credit. The TODO list shows an image and release date per entry. Sending a whole-series gap to Sonarr from a filmography, recommendation, or favorites entry sends the series' own title rather than the name of whatever surfaced it, and a rejected Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr request shows the service's validation message instead of a raw response body.

10.11.8.0 - The Gaps Report is reorganized around your library's domains: Movies, Shows, Music, and Books are now the primary tabs, each badged with its own gap count, with Set completion, Creator works, and Discover scoped underneath as a view you pick per domain, so only the active domain's data is loaded at a time.
